units.zh: 昔者元胎無象，太素流形，對越在天，以爲元首，則記所謂冬居營窟，夏居橧巢，飲血茹毛，未有麻絲者也。
units.en: In the earliest age, before form coalesced from undivided simplicity, people already looked toward heaven as their sovereign; the old annals picture them wintering in earthen dens, summering in treetop huts, living on raw flesh and blood, long before cloth ever softened their lives.
units.literal: In antiquity the primordial embryo had no image; Grand Simplicity flowed into forms; facing and answering what is on high, they took it as the supreme head—then the records say they dwelt in burrows in winter and nests in summer, drank blood and ate fur, and had not yet hemp or silk.

units.zh: 及燧人鑽火，庖犧出震，風宗下武，炎胤昌基，畫野無聞，其歸一揆。
units.en: Then Suiren struck fire from wood, Fuxi rose in the east like thunder, wind and flame passed their line down to martial kings, and the royal house widened its base; we hear nothing yet of surveying fields into squares, but every step still aimed at the same single standard of rule.
units.literal: When Suiren drilled fire, Paoxi emerged in the Zhen (east) trigram; the Feng lineage descended to the martial kings, and the Yan heirs broadened the foundation; dividing the wilds is not heard of—their return is one measure.

units.zh: 黃帝則東海南江，登空躡岱，至於崑峰振轡，崆山訪道，[1]存諸汗竹，不可厚誣。
units.en: The Yellow Emperor pressed east to the sea and south along the great streams, climbed Kongsang and crossed Mount Tai, climbed Kunlun to tighten his reins and sought the Way on Kongshan; the fact is inked on bamboo that has soaked in human sweat, and it would be perverse to dismiss it as mere legend.
units.literal: As for the Yellow Emperor: east to the sea, south to the great rivers; ascending hollow (Kong) and treading Dai; reaching Kun peaks to shake the reins, Kongshan to inquire of the Way—[1] it is preserved on sweating bamboo strips and cannot be heavily slandered.

units.zh: 高陽任地依神，帝嚳順天行義。
units.en: Zhuanxu, the High Yang line, grounded his power in the land and the spirits; Emperor Ku shaped policy by heaven's pattern and the moral law.
units.literal: Gaoyang relied on earth and depended on spirits; Emperor Ku followed heaven and practiced righteousness.

units.zh: 東踰蟠木，西濟流沙，北至幽陵，南撫交阯，日月所經，舟車所至，莫匪王臣，不踰茲域。
units.en: Their sway ran east past the curling forest, west across the shifting sands, north to the cold marches, south to the Red River delta—every place the sun and moon lit and every road a wheel could find lay inside the ring of royal subjects, and nothing beyond that ring counted as theirs.
units.literal: East they crossed Panmu, west they forded the flowing sands, north they reached Youling, south they soothed Jiaozhi; wherever sun and moon passed, wherever boat and cart could reach, none were not the king's subjects—they did not overstep this domain.

units.zh: 帝堯時，禹平水土，以爲九州。
units.en: Under Emperor Yao, Yu drained the flood and settled the soil, and from that labor the Nine Provinces took their shape.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Yao, Yu pacified the waters and earth, and thereby made the nine provinces.

units.zh: 虞舜登庸，厥功彌劭，表提類而分區宇，判山河而考疆域，冀北創并部之名，燕齊起幽營之號，則書所謂肇十有二州，封十有二山者也。
units.en: Once Shun took office, his achievement only deepened: he sorted kinds of terrain, carved the realm into regions, traced ranges and rivers to fix true borders, split the northern Ji plain to name the Bing command, and gave Yan and Qi the new titles of You and Ying—exactly the twelve provinces and twelve sacred peaks the classics say he first ordained.
units.literal: When Shun of Yu ascended to employment, his merit grew ever greater; he displayed categories and divided the regional cosmos, adjudicated mountains and rivers and examined boundaries; north of Ji he created the name of the Bing department; in Yan and Qi he raised the designations of You and Ying—this is what the documents call initiating twelve provinces and enfeoffing twelve mountains.

units.zh: 夏功在于唐堯，殷因無所損益。
units.en: The Xia built on the work of Yao of Tang; the Shang inherited that map and left its proportions unchanged.
units.literal: The Xia's achievement lay in Tang-Yao; the Yin inherited and had nothing to diminish or increase.

units.en: When King Wu of Zhou overthrew the Shang, he moved the seat of power from Feng to Hao.
units.literal: King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, from Feng going to Hao.

units.zh: 至成王時，改作禹貢，徐梁入於青雍，冀野析於幽并。
units.en: Under King Cheng the court rewrote the "Tribute of Yu" grid: Xu and Liang were folded into Qing and Yong, while the old Ji heartland was carved into new You and Bing sectors.
units.literal: By the time of King Cheng, they revised and made the Tribute of Yu; Xu and Liang were absorbed into Qing and Yong; the wilds of Ji were split into You and Bing.

units.zh: 職方掌天下之土，以周厥利；
units.en: The Bureau of Domains held the register of every soil under heaven, weighing what each tract could yield;
units.literal: The Office of Regions grasped the soil of all under heaven, in order to complete its advantages;

units.zh: 保章辯九州之野，皆有分星。
units.en: The star-masters matched each of the Nine Provinces to its own stretch of sky, every region with its allotted constellation.
units.literal: The Star-Clerk distinguished the wilds of the nine provinces; each had apportioned stars.

units.zh: 東南曰揚州，正南曰荊州，河南曰豫州，正東曰青州，河東曰兗州，正西曰雍州，東北曰幽州，河內曰冀州，正北曰并州。
units.en: The southeast quarter was Yangzhou, the south face Jingzhou, the ground south of the Yellow River Yuzhou, the east face Qingzhou, the ground east of the river Yanzhou, the west face Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, the inner bend of the river Jizhou, and the north face Bingzhou.
units.literal: The southeast is called Yangzhou, the due south Jingzhou, south of the river Yuzhou, the due east Qingzhou, east of the river Yanzhou, the due west Yongzhou, the northeast Youzhou, within the river Jizhou, the due north Bingzhou.

units.zh: 始皇初并天下，懲{乂心}戰國，削罷列侯，分天下爲三十六郡。
units.en: The First Emperor, fresh from unifying the realm and determined not to repeat Warring States chaos, stripped the old enfeoffed nobles of power and carved the empire into thirty-six commanderies.
units.literal: When the First Emperor first united all under heaven, chastened by the Warring States, he cut away and abolished the ranked feudal lords and divided all under heaven into thirty-six commanderies.

units.zh: 〈三川、河東、南陽、南郡、九江、鄣郡、會稽、潁川、碭郡、泗水、薛郡、東郡、琅邪、齊郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、遼西、遼東、代郡、鉅鹿、邯鄲、上黨、太原、雲中、九原、雁門、上郡、隴西、北地、漢中、巴郡、蜀郡、黔中、長沙，凡三十五郡，與內史爲三十六郡也。〉
units.en: 〈The thirty-five commanderies were Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, Xue, Dong, Langye, Qi, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba, Shu, Qianzhong, and Changsha; together with the metropolitan intendant's district, they made thirty-six commanderies.〉
units.literal: 〈Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Nanjun, Jiujiang, Zhang commandery, Kuaiji, Yingchuan, Dang commandery, Sishui, Xue commandery, Dong commandery, Langye, Qi commandery, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, Liaodong, Dai commandery, Julu, Handan, Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Yanmen, Shang commandery, Longxi, Beidi, Hanzhong, Ba commandery, Shu commandery, Qianzhong, Changsha—in all thirty-five commanderies, which together with the metropolitan intendant made thirty-six commanderies.〉

units.zh: 於是興師踰江，平取百越，又置閩中、南海、桂林、象郡，凡四十郡，郡一守焉。
units.en: He then sent armies south of the Yangtze, crushed the Yue peoples, and added Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang, bringing the whole system to forty commanderies, each overseen by a single appointed governor.
units.literal: Thereupon they raised armies and crossed the rivers, pacified and took the Hundred Yue, and further established Minzhong, Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies—in all forty commanderies, each commandery having one governor.

units.zh: 其地則西臨洮而北沙漠，東縈西帶，皆臨大海。
units.en: The new realm ran west to the Tao River and north to the sands, while east and south it looped like a sash until every outer edge touched the sea.
units.literal: As for the territory: west it bordered Tao and north the desert; east winding, west belting—all bordered the great sea.

units.zh: 漢祖龍興，革秦之弊，分內史爲三部，更置郡國二十有三，
units.en: When the Han founder seized the mandate, he undid Qin's excesses, split the old inner intendant into three metropolitan circuits, and added twenty-three new commanderies and princely kingdoms,
units.literal: The Han progenitor rose like a dragon, reformed the Qin's abuses, divided the metropolitan intendant into three parts, and further established twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,

units.zh: 〈桂陽、江夏、豫章、河內、魏郡、東海、楚國、平原、梁國、定襄、泰山、汝南、淮陽、千乘、東萊、燕國、清河、信都、常山、中山、渤海、廣漢、涿郡，合二十三也。
units.en: 〈These were Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei, Donghai, Chu, Pingyuan, Liang, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, and Zhuo, twenty-three in all.
units.literal: 〈Guiyang, Jiangxia, Yuzhang, Henei, Wei commandery, Donghai, Chu kingdom, Pingyuan, Liang kingdom, Dingxiang, Taishan, Runan, Huaiyang, Qiansheng, Donglai, Yan kingdom, Qinghe, Xindu, Changshan, Zhongshan, Bohai, Guanghan, Zhuo commandery—together twenty-three.

units.zh: 三內史者，河上、渭南、中地也。
units.en: The three inner districts were Heshang south of the bend, Weinan, and the central capital belt.
units.literal: The three metropolitan intendants are: Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi.

units.zh: 地理志曰：高祖增二十六，武帝改河上、渭南、中地以爲京兆、馮翊、扶風，是爲三輔也。〉
units.en: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—these are the Three Adjuncts.〉
units.literal: The Treatise on Geography says: Gaozu added twenty-six; Emperor Wu changed Heshang, Weinan, and Zhongdi into Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng—this is the Three Adjuncts.〉

units.en: Emperor Wen of Han added nine more,
units.literal: Wen added thereto nine,

units.zh: 〈廣平、城陽、淄川、濟南、膠西、膠東、河間、廬江、衡山，武帝改衡山曰「六安」。〉
units.en: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, and Hengshan—the last of which Emperor Wu renamed "Liu'an."〉
units.literal: 〈Guangping, Chengyang, Zichuan, Jinan, Jiaoxi, Jiaodong, Hejian, Lujiang, Hengshan—Emperor Wu changed Hengshan to "Liu'an."〉

units.en: Emperor Jing added four more.
units.literal: Jing added four of them.

units.en: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.
units.literal: 〈Jibei, Jiyin, Shanyang, and Beihai.

units.en: Emperor Xuan renamed Jibei as Dongping.〉
units.literal: Xuan changed Jibei to Dongping.〉

units.zh: 武帝開越攘胡，初置十七，
units.en: Emperor Wu campaigned south against Yue and north against the steppe peoples, and his first expansion added seventeen commanderies,
units.literal: Emperor Wu opened the Yue and pushed back the Hu, at first establishing seventeen,

units.zh: 〈南海、蒼梧、鬱林、合浦、交阯、九真、日南、珠崖、儋耳九郡，平西南夷置牂柯、越巂、沈黎、汶山、犍爲、益州六郡，西置武都郡，又分立零陵郡，合十七郡。〉
units.en: 〈nine southern coast commands from Nanhai to Dan'er, six carved from the southwest Yi heartland, Wudu on the western flank, and a split Lingling—seventeen new units in that push.〉
units.literal: 〈Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan, Zhuya, Dan'er—nine commanderies; pacifying the southwestern Yi, established Zangke, Yuexi, Chenli, Wenshan, Qianwei, Yizhou—six commanderies; west established Wudu commandery; again separately established Lingling commandery—together seventeen commanderies.〉

units.en: Further conquests widened the map by fourteen more commanderies.
units.literal: Expanding soil and dividing boundaries, again added fourteen.

units.zh: 〈弘農、臨淮、西河、朔方、酒泉、陳留、安定、天水、玄菟、樂浪、廣陵、敦煌、武威、張掖。〉
units.en: 〈The fourteen interior and frontier commanderies were Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, and Zhangye.〉
units.literal: 〈Hongnong, Linhuai, Xihe, Shuofang, Jiuquan, Chenliu, Anding, Tianshui, Xuantu, Lelang, Guangling, Dunhuang, Wuwei, Zhangye.〉

units.en: Under the short reign of Emperor Zhao the court added only one more.
units.literal: Emperor Zhao had few undertakings, again added one thereof.

units.en: 〈Jincheng commandery.〉
units.literal: 〈Jincheng.〉

units.zh: 至平帝元始二年，凡新置郡國七十有一，與秦四十，合一百一十有一。
units.en: By the second year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, Han had founded seventy-one new units; added to Qin's forty, the roster stood at one hundred eleven.
units.literal: Down to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year, in all newly established commanderies and kingdoms were seventy-one; together with Qin's forty, altogether one hundred eleven.

units.zh: 改雍曰涼，改梁曰益，又置徐州，復夏舊號，南置交阯，北有朔方，凡爲十三部。
units.en: Yong was changed to Liang, Liang to Yi; Xuzhou was further established; Xia's old designations were restored; Jiaozhi was set up in the south and Shuofang in the north—thirteen departments in all.
units.literal: Changed Yong to Liang, changed Liang to Yi, further established Xuzhou, restored Xia's old designations, south established Jiaozhi, north had Shuofang—in all became thirteen departments.

units.zh: 〈涼、益、荊、揚、青、豫、兗、徐、幽、并、冀十一州，交阯、朔方二刺史，合十三部。〉
units.en: 〈Eleven provinces from Liang to Ji plus two special zones, Jiaozhi and Shuofang, each with its own regional commissioner—thirteen departments in all.〉
units.literal: 〈Liang, Yi, Jing, Yang, Qing, Yu, Yan, Xu, You, Bing, Ji—eleven provinces; Jiaozhi, Shuofang—two regional inspectors; together thirteen departments.〉

units.zh: 光武投戈之歲，在彫秏之辰，郡國蕭條，并省者八。
units.en: When Guangwu laid down the sword, the realm was gaunt from war; eight redundant commanderies were folded away in the general retrenchment.
units.literal: In the year Guangwu cast aside the spear, it was a time of wasting exhaustion; commanderies and kingdoms were desolate; those merged and abolished were eight.

units.zh: 〈城陽、淄川、高密、膠東、六安、真定、泗水、廣陽。〉
units.en: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, and Guangyang were the eight struck from the map.〉
units.literal: 〈Chengyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, Jiaodong, Liu'an, Zhending, Sishui, Guangyang.〉

units.zh: 建武十一年，省州牧，復爲刺史，員十三人，各掌一州。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Jianwu the court abolished the provincial governorships, restored classic regional censors, and fixed their number at thirteen, one to each major province.
units.literal: Jianwu eleventh year, abolished provincial shepherds, again became censors; establishment thirteen men, each grasping one province.

units.en: Emperor Ming added one seat,
units.literal: Mingdi established one,

units.en: 〈Yongchang in the far southwest.〉
units.literal: 〈Yongchang.〉

units.en: Emperor Zhang added two commands,
units.literal: Zhangdi established two,

units.en: 〈Rencheng and Wu commandery.〉
units.literal: 〈Rencheng, Wu commandery.〉

units.en: Under Emperors He and Shun names were altered; there were nine of them.
units.literal: He and Shun altered and made; their names were nine.

units.zh: 〈和置濟北、廣陽，順改淮陽爲陳，改楚爲彭城，濟東爲東平，臨淮爲下邳，千乘爲六安，信都爲安平，天水爲漢陽。〉
units.en: 〈Emperor He revived Jibei and Guangyang; Emperor Shun renamed Huaiyang as Chen, the old Chu core as Pengcheng, Jidong as Dongping, Linhuai as Xiapi, Qiansheng as Liu'an, Xindu as Anping, and Tianshui as Hanyang.〉
units.literal: 〈He established Jibei and Guangyang; Shun changed Huaiyang to Chen, changed Chu to Pengcheng, Jidong to Dongping, Linhuai to Xiapi, Qiansheng to Liu'an, Xindu to Anping, Tianshui to Hanyang.〉

units.zh: 省朔方刺史，合之於司隸，凡十三部，
units.en: Shuofang's inspectorate was folded into the capital superintendent's zone, leaving thirteen departments in the Eastern Han scheme,
units.literal: Abolished the Shuofang regional inspector, merged it into the Metropolitan Superintendent; in all thirteen departments,

units.zh: 〈其與西漢不同者，司隸校尉部郡治河南，朔方隸於并部。〉
units.en: 〈Unlike Western Han, the metropolitan belt was administered from Henan, while Shuofang answered to the Bing inspector rather than standing alone.〉
units.literal: 〈Where it differs from Western Han: the Metropolitan Superintendent's commandery-administered region takes Henan as its seat; Shuofang is subordinate to Bing department.〉

units.en: The Eastern Han roster thus held one hundred eight commanderies and kingdoms.
units.literal: And commanderies and kingdoms were one hundred eight.

units.zh: 〈省前漢八，分置五，改舊名七，因舊九十六，少前漢三也。〉
units.en: 〈Eight Western Han units were cut, five new ones split off, seven were simply renamed, ninety-six kept their old titles—three fewer than the old Han total.〉
units.literal: 〈Abolished eight of Former Han, split and established five, changed old names seven, continued old ninety-six—three fewer than Former Han.〉

units.zh: 桓靈頗增於前，復置六郡。
units.en: Under Emperors Huan and Ling the court added six commanderies beyond the earlier baseline.
units.literal: Huan and Ling somewhat increased over before, again established six commanderies.

units.en: 〈Emperor Huan created Gaoyang, Gaoliang, and Boling;
units.literal: 〈Huan: Gaoyang, Gaoliang, Boling;

units.en: Emperor Ling added Nan'an, Poyang, and Luling.〉
units.literal: Ling: Nan'an, Poyang, Luling.〉

units.zh: 魏武定霸，三方鼎立，生靈版蕩，關洛荒蕪，所置者十二，
units.en: When Wei Wu settled his hegemony, the three sides stood like a tripod, the people were thrown into turmoil, the passes and Luo region lay desolate, and those he established were twelve,
units.literal: Wei Wu settled hegemony; the three sides stood like a tripod; living beings were on tablet-like upheaval; Guan and Luo were desolate; those established were twelve,

units.zh: 〈新興、樂平、西平、新平、略陽、陰平、帶方、譙、樂陵、章武、南鄉、襄陽。〉
units.en: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, and Xiangyang.〉
units.literal: 〈Xinxing, Leping, Xiping, Xinping, Lueyang, Yinping, Daifang, Qiao, Leling, Zhangwu, Nanxiang, Xiangyang.〉

units.en: Seven older commands were struck at the same time,
units.literal: Those abolished were seven,

units.zh: 〈上郡、朔方、五原、雲中、定襄、漁陽、廬江。〉
units.en: 〈Shang, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, and Lujiang were the seven removed.〉
units.literal: 〈Shang commandery, Shuofang, Wuyuan, Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Yuyang, Lujiang.〉

units.en: Emperor Wen of Wei then added seven more,
units.literal: And Wendi established seven,

units.zh: 〈朝歌、陽平、弋陽、魏興、新城、義陽、[2]安豐。〉
units.en: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉
units.literal: 〈Zhaoge, Yangping, the Ru-nan Yiyang, Weixing, Xincheng, the Huai-line Yiyang, and Anfeng.〉

units.en: Emperor Ming and the first boy emperor each added one commandery—two in all,
units.literal: Ming and the Lesser Emperor added two,

units.en: 〈Mingdi restored Shangyong;
units.literal: 〈Ming: Shangyong;

units.en: the boy emperor added Pingyang.〉
units.literal: Lesser: Pingyang.〉

units.en: Wei thus held fifty-four commanderies inherited from Han.
units.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were fifty-four.

units.zh: 蜀先主於漢建安之間初置郡九，
units.en: Between the Jian'an years, Liu Bei in Shu-Han first carved out nine commanderies,
units.literal: Shu's First Sovereign, in the interval of Han's Jian'an, first established nine commanderies,

units.zh: 〈巴東、巴西、梓潼、江陽、汶山、漢嘉、朱提、宕渠、涪陵。〉
units.en: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, and Fuling.〉
units.literal: 〈Badong, Baxi, Zitong, Jiangyang, Wenshan, Hanjia, Zhuti, Dangqu, Fuling.〉

units.en: Liu Shan later added two more,
units.literal: The Later Sovereign added two,

units.en: 〈Yunnan and Xingu in the far south.〉
units.literal: 〈Yunnan, Xingu.〉

units.en: Shu ultimately held eleven Han-era commanderies.
units.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eleven.

units.en: Sun Quan, Wu's Great Emperor, first founded five commanderies,
units.literal: The Wu ruler, the Great Emperor, first established five commanderies,

units.zh: 〈臨賀、武昌、珠崖、新安、廬陵南部。〉
units.en: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, and the southern annex of Luling.〉
units.literal: 〈Linhe, Wuchang, Zhuya, Xin'an, southern Luling.〉

units.en: Sun Liang and Sun Xiu each added four commanderies,
units.literal: The Lesser Emperor and Emperor Jing each four,

units.en: 〈Sun Liang created Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, and Xiangdong;
units.literal: 〈Lesser: Linchuan, Linhai, Hengyang, Xiangdong.

units.zh: 景，天門、建安、建平、合浦北部。〉
units.en: Sun Xiu added Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, and northern Hepu.〉
units.literal: Jing: Tianmen, Jian'an, Jianping, northern Hepu.〉

units.en: Sun Hao, the "Marquis Who Surrendered His Mandate," still ordered twelve more commanderies founded,
units.literal: The Marquis Who Submits to Fate also established twelve commanderies,

units.zh: 〈始安、始興、邵陵、安成、新昌、武平、九德、吳興、東陽、桂林、滎陽、宜都。〉
units.en: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, and Yidu.〉
units.literal: 〈Shi'an, Shixing, Shaoling, Ancheng, Xinchang, Wuping, Jiude, Wuxing, Dongyang, Guilin, Yingyang, Yidu.〉

units.en: Wu in the end controlled eighteen commanderies that had once belonged to Han.
units.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eighteen.

units.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，既平孫氏，凡增置郡國二十有三，
units.en: In the first year of Taikang, after Jin Wudi crushed the Sun regime, the court created twenty-three new commanderies and kingdoms,
units.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Taikang first year, having already pacified the Sun clan, in all added twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,

units.zh: 〈滎陽、上洛、頓丘、臨淮、東莞、襄城、汝陰、長廣、廣甯、昌黎、新野、隨郡、陰平、義陽、毗陵、宣城、南康、晉安、寧浦、始平、略陽、樂平、南平。〉
units.en: 〈The twenty-three units were Yingyang, Shangluo, Dunqiu, Linhuai, Dongguan, Xiangcheng, Ru'yin, Changguang, Guangning, Changli, Xinye, Sui, Yinping, Yiyang, Piling, Xuancheng, Nankang, Jin'an, Ningpu, Shiping, Lueyang, Leping, and Nanping.〉
units.literal: 〈Yingyang, Shangluo, Dunqiu, Linhuai, Dongguan, Xiangcheng, Ru'yin, Changguang, Guangning, Changli, Xinye, Sui commandery, Yinping, Yiyang, Piling, Xuancheng, Nankang, Jin'an, Ningpu, Shiping, Lueyang, Leping, Nanping.〉

units.zh: 省司隸置司州，別立梁、秦、寧、平四州，仍吳之廣州，凡十九州，
units.en: The old metropolitan belt became Sizhou, Liang, Qin, Ning, and Ping were spun off as new provinces, Wu's Guangzhou was kept, and the empire was reorganized into nineteen provinces,
units.literal: Abolished the Metropolitan Superintendent and established Sizhou; separately established Liang, Qin, Ning, and Ping four provinces; continued Wu's Guangzhou—in all nineteen provinces,

units.zh: 〈司、冀、兗、豫、荊、徐、揚、青、幽、平、并、雍、涼、秦、梁、益、寧、交、廣州。〉
units.en: 〈Si through Guang—the nineteen names that now girdled the reunited realm.〉
units.literal: 〈Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, Xu, Yang, Qing, You, Ping, Bing, Yong, Liang (Hexi), Qin, Liang (Hanzhong), Yi, Ning, Jiao, Guang provinces.〉

units.en: The commandery and kingdom count stood at one hundred seventy-three,
units.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms one hundred seventy-three,

units.zh: 〈仍吳所置二十五，仍蜀新置十一，仍魏所置二十一，仍漢舊九十三，置二十三。〉
units.en: 〈Twenty-five Wu foundations, eleven Shu additions, twenty-one Wei creations, ninety-three Han survivals, and twenty-three brand-new Jin seats.〉
units.literal: 〈Continued twenty-five set by Wu, continued eleven newly set by Shu, continued twenty-one set by Wei, continued ninety-three old Han ones, established twenty-three.〉

units.zh: 以爲冠帶之國，盡有殷周之土。
units.en: Jin now wore the full cap-and-girdle dignity of the central states and held every tract the Yin and Zhou kings had once claimed.
units.literal: Thereby making the cap-and-belt states; fully possessing the soil of Yin and Zhou.

units.zh: 若乃敦龐於天地之始，昭晰於犧農之世，用長黎元，未爭疆埸。
units.en: In the first mists of creation life spread in generous abundance; under Fuxi and Shennong the world grew plain and bright, and the people multiplied long before anyone quarreled over furrows on a map.
units.literal: As for being rich and vast at heaven and earth's beginning, bright and clear in the age of Xi and Shennong, thereby lengthening the black-haired people—not yet contending over border fields.

units.zh: 而玉環楛矢，夷裘風駕，南翬表貺，東風入律，光乎上德，奚遠弗臻。
units.en: Jade rings and blunt arrows, furs from forest peoples, embassies riding the seasonal winds, southern birds offered as tribute, eastern breezes tuning the pitch-pipes—all of it proclaimed a sovereign virtue so luminous that no corner of the map stayed beyond reach.
units.literal: Moreover jade rings and blunt-arrow tribute, Yi furs and wind-borne carriages, southern pheasant-plumes displaying gifts, east wind entering the pitch-pipes—shining with high virtue, what distant place did not arrive?

units.zh: 然則星象麗天，山河紀地，端掖裁其弘敞，崤函判其都邑，仰觀俯察，萬物攸歸。
units.en: Stars lace the sky while mountains and rivers score the earth; palace avenues pace out the capital's grandeur, the Xiao and Han passes mark where dynasties chose to sit—look up or down and every creature finds its place inside that frame.
units.literal: Thus then star-patterns attach to heaven, mountains and rivers record earth; the layered palace avenues bound their vast breadth, the Xiao and Han passes mark their capitals; looking up, looking down, the myriad things have their return.

units.zh: 是以洛沚咸陽，宛然秦漢，晉濱河西，同知堯禹，于茲新邑，宅是鎬京，五尺童子皆能口誦者，史官弗之書也。
units.en: Everyone nods when you name the Luo shoals or Xianyang as the heart of Qin and Han, or liken Jin's hold on the western riverbank to the world Yao and Yu knew; every schoolchild can chant how the new capital sits where Haojing once stood—truths so worn smooth by memory that the official annals pass them by in silence.
units.literal: Therefore Luozhi and Xianyang, just so Qin and Han; Jin along the west of the river, likewise knowing Yao and Yu; at this new city, dwelling is Haojing—what even a five-foot child can recite from memory, the historiographers do not write thereof.

units.zh: 昔庖犧氏生於成紀，而爲天子，都於陳。
units.en: Legend places Fuxi's birth at Chenji; he became Son of Heaven and made his capital at Chen.
units.literal: Formerly Paoxi was born at Chenji and became Son of Heaven, with capital at Chen.

units.zh: 神農氏都陳，而別營于曲阜。
units.en: Shennong ruled from Chen yet pitched a second court at Qufu.
units.literal: Shennong took Chen as capital, but separately encamped at Qufu.

units.zh: 黃帝生於壽丘，而都於涿鹿。
units.en: The Yellow Emperor was born on Shouqiu hill and built his capital at Zhuolu.
units.literal: The Yellow Emperor was born at Shouqiu, but had capital at Zhuolu.

units.zh: 少昊始自窮桑，而遷都曲阜。
units.en: Shaohao rose from Qiongsang and later shifted his seat to Qufu.
units.literal: Shaohao began from Qiongsang, but moved the capital to Qufu.

units.zh: 顓頊始自窮桑，而徙邑商丘。
units.en: Zhuanxu likewise started from Qiongsang before relocating his capital to Shangqiu.
units.literal: Zhuanxu began from Qiongsang, but moved the town to Shangqiu.

units.en: Gaoxin took the throne-name and founded his capital at Bo.
units.literal: Gaoxin assumed the title, established capital at Bo.

units.zh: 孫卿子曰：「不登高山，不知天之高；
units.en: Xunzi wrote, "Unless you climb a high peak you cannot grasp how high the sky hangs;
units.literal: Master Xun Qing said: "If you do not climb a high mountain, you do not know heaven's height;

units.zh: 不臨深谿，不知地之厚也。」
units.en: unless you stand above a deep gorge you cannot feel how thick the earth runs beneath you."
units.literal: if you do not overlook a deep ravine, you do not know earth's thickness."

units.zh: 大哉坤象，萬物資生，載崑華而不墜，傾河海而寧泄。
units.en: Vast is the earth's emblem in the Changes: every creature draws life from it; it shoulders Kunlun and Mount Hua without collapsing, and even when the Yellow River and the sea pour through it, the land does not burst.
units.literal: Great is the kun trigram's image; the myriad things rely on it for life; it bears Kunlun and Mount Hua without falling; it tilts the rivers and seas yet is calm in draining."

units.zh: 考卜惟王，乘飛駐軫，睨𡹮山而鐫勒，覽曾城以爲玩。
units.en: Kings read the tortoise cracks, raced chariots to the ends of the roads, squinted up at Minshan and carved boastful stelae, and treated terraced capitals as baubles.
units.literal: Divining tortoise-shells for the king, riding flight halting at the axle-ends, gazing askance at Min mountains and carving inscriptions, viewing layered towers as playthings.

units.zh: 時逢稽浸，道接陵夷，平王東遷，星離豆剖，當塗馭宇，瓜分鼎立。
units.en: Then came years of flood and dearth, the royal Way slid downhill, Pingwang fled east and the realm shattered like stars and pods, the Caos seized the chariot-reins, and the land was carved into three rival stoves.
units.literal: Times encountered famine-floods; the Way met decline; King Ping moved east; stars scattered, beans split; the cart-track clan grasped the cosmos; melons divided, tripod stood apart.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝接千祀之餘，當八堯之禪，先王桑梓，罄宇來歸，斯固可得而言者矣。
units.en: Our martial founding emperor, Shizu, picked up the threads after a thousand years of sacrifice, stood in the moment of a mandate-shift worthy of Yao's age, and watched the old heartland—the mulberry-and-catalpa home of the kings—empty itself back into his hands; that much, at least, can be told aloud.
units.literal: Shizu Emperor Wu took up the remainder after a thousand sacrifices, faced the abdication like the eight Yao transfers; the Former Kings' mulberry and catalpa— the whole realm came to return—this indeed can be spoken of.

units.zh: 惠皇不虞，中州盡棄，永嘉南度，綸行建鄴，九分天下而有二焉。
units.en: When Emperor Hui fell to calamity the Central Plain was lost; after the Yongjia flight south the court set its capital at Jianye by imperial decree, holding barely two shares of a realm once counted in ninths.
units.literal: Emperor Hui met unexpected disaster; the central plain was wholly abandoned; Yongjia southward crossing, by edict-progress establishing Jiankang; of nine parts of all under heaven they had two.

units.zh: 昔大禹觀於濁河而受綠字，寰瀛之內可得而言也。
units.en: Long ago Yu the Great stood by the silty Yellow River and read the green script that mapped the world; inside the belt of the oceans every place can finally be named.
units.literal: Formerly Great Yu gazed on the muddy Yellow River and received the green characters; within the ring of the seas it can be spoken of.

units.en: Seven stellar mansions hang above, and seven terrestrial markers answer them below;
units.literal: Heaven has seven stars; earth has seven markers;

units.en: The sky is hung on four cosmic stays, and the land is gouged by four mighty watercourses that carry the flood away.
units.literal: Heaven has four sustaining cords (weft/bindings); earth has four great draining channels.

units.en: Beyond the encircling girdle that ropes in the known world lie the eight outermost reaches.
units.literal: Outside the eight cords of the world, they are called the eight extremities.

units.zh: 地不足東南，天不足西北。
units.en: The ground gives way to the southeast, while the empyrean gapes widest toward the northwest.
units.literal: Earth falls short toward the southeast; heaven falls short toward the northwest.

units.zh: 八極之廣，東西二億三萬一千三百里，南北二億三萬一千三百里。
units.en: From the eastern pole to the western spans two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li—and the same measure runs from south to north.
units.literal: The breadth of the eight extremities: east and west, two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li; north and south, likewise two hundred thirty-one thousand three hundred li.

units.zh: 自地至天，半八極之數，自下亦如之。
units.en: The vault above measured half the span of the Eight Poles, and the same depth echoed below.
units.literal: From earth to heaven is half the tally of the eight extremities; from below upward it is likewise.

units.zh: 昔黃帝令豎亥步自東極，至于西極，五億十萬九千八百八步。
units.en: Once the Yellow Emperor bade Shu Hai stride from sunrise to sunset; the tally came to five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight measured paces.
units.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor ordered Shu Hai to pace from the eastern extremity to the western extremity: five hundred nine thousand eight hundred eight paces.

units.zh: 史臣案，凡周天積百七萬九百一十三里，徑三十五萬六千九百七十里。
units.en: Court mathematicians reckoned heaven's circuit at 1,070,913 li and its diameter at 356,970 li.
units.literal: The court historiographers ascertain: in all the circumference of heaven totals one million seventy thousand nine hundred thirteen li; the diameter is three hundred fifty-six thousand nine hundred seventy li.

units.zh: 所謂南北爲經，東西爲緯。
units.en: This is what is meant by naming north-south the warp and east-west the weft.
units.literal: That which is called: north-south as warp, east-west as weft.

units.zh: 天有十二次，日月之所躔；
units.en: Twelve lunar lodges score the sky—the highway of sun and moon;
units.literal: Heaven has twelve celestial lodges; they are where the sun and moon tread their circuits;

units.zh: 地有十二辰，王侯之所國也。
units.en: twelve earthly divisions underpin the map where lords and princes plant their altars of soil and grain.
units.literal: earth has twelve earthly branches; they are where kings and marquises establish states.

units.zh: 或因生得姓，因功命土，祁、酉、燕、齊，在乎茲域。
units.en: Some clans took names from ancestral seats, others earned fiefs for deeds done—and the old domains of Qi (the Qi clan), You, Yan, and Qi (the eastern state) all fall inside these bounds.
units.literal: Some by birth obtain surnames, by merit receive land; Qi, You, Yan, and Qi lie within this region.

units.zh: 昔黃帝旁行天下，方制萬里，得百里之國萬區，則《周易》所謂「首出庶物，萬國咸寧」者也。
units.en: Long ago the Yellow Emperor quartered the realm, squared a domain ten thousand li on a side, and carved it into ten thousand hundred-li polities—the very epoch the Book of Changes extols when it says, "He who rises first above the throng brings every kingdom to rest."
units.literal: Formerly the Yellow Emperor traveled the realm in all directions, regulated a square of ten thousand li, and obtained ten thousand regions of hundred-li states—this is what the Zhou Yi calls "first emerging among the myriad things; the myriad states all attain tranquility."

units.zh: 昔在帝堯，協和萬邦，制八家爲鄰，三鄰爲朋，三朋爲里，五里爲邑，十邑爲都，十都爲師，州十有二師焉。
units.en: Under Yao the countries learned concord, and government knit tight: eight families made a street, three streets a cluster, three clusters a ward, five wards a market town, ten such towns a greater burgh, ten burghs a canton, and twelve cantons stitched one province.
units.literal: Formerly under Emperor Yao he harmonized the myriad states; he regulated: eight households form a neighborhood, three neighborhoods form a peng, three peng form a li, five li form a yi, ten yi form a du, ten du form a shi, and a province has twelve shi.

units.zh: 夏后氏東漸于海，西被于流沙，南浮于江，而朔南暨聲教，窮豎亥所步，莫不率俾，會群臣於塗山，執玉帛者萬國。
units.en: The Xia stretched east until the tide foamed at their feet, west to the shifting sands, south along the great rivers, until their transforming influence ran from pole to pole as far as Shu Hai had ever measured; none refused homage. At Mount Tu they gathered the lords, and ten thousand courts arrived with jade disks and silk.
units.literal: The house of Xia eastward reached to the sea, westward extended to the flowing sands, southward floated on the Jiang; north and south likewise were united by culture and teaching, exhausting where Shu Hai had paced; none failed to follow and obey; they assembled the host of lords at Tu Shan; those bearing jade and silk were ten thousand states.

units.zh: 於是九州之內，作爲五服。
units.en: Within the Nine Provinces they layered five concentric belts of fealty.
units.literal: Thereupon within the nine provinces they established the five domains (fu).

units.zh: 天子之國，內五百里甸服，百里賦納總，二百里納銍，三百里納秸服，四百里粟，五百里米。
units.en: Around the capital ran five hundred li of royal fields: the inner ring sent whole stalks bundled, the next matured heads, the third straw and labor, the fourth threshed grain, the outermost polished rice for the palace kettle.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's state: the inner five hundred li is the royal domain; at one hundred li tribute is delivered as bound sheaves in the husk; at two hundred li sickle-cut ears; at three hundred li straw and corvée service; at four hundred li millet; at five hundred li rice.

units.zh: 甸服外五百里侯服，百里采，二百里任，三百里候。
units.en: Beyond that stretched another five hundred li of baronial land: the first hundred fed royal manors, the next two hundred supplied ministers of trust, the outer three hundred patrolled the marches.
units.literal: Outside the royal domain, five hundred li of marquis-domain: one hundred li of estates, two hundred li of appointments, three hundred li of garrison/watch.

units.zh: 侯服外五百里綏服，三百里揆文教，二百里奮武衛。
units.en: Next came five hundred li meant to "soothe": three hundred for schools and rites, two hundred bristling with spears that guarded the cordon.
units.literal: Outside the marquis-domain, five hundred li of pacification-domain: three hundred li for adjusting civil teaching and rites, two hundred li for vigorous martial guard.

units.zh: 綏服外五百里要服，三百里夷，二百里蔡。
units.en: Outside the pacified belt lay five hundred li of "treaty" ground—three hundred li of loosely ruled bordermen, two hundred more under banishment law.
units.literal: Outside the pacification-domain, five hundred li of binding-domain: three hundred li of outer Yi, two hundred li of Cai.

units.zh: 要服外五百里荒服，三百里蠻，二百里流。
units.en: The rim was five hundred li of wilderness—three hundred left to rough hill tribes, two hundred reserved for the river of banishment.
units.literal: Outside the binding-domain, five hundred li of wild-domain: three hundred li of Man, two hundred li of exile-flow.

units.zh: 訖于四海，弼成五服，五服至于五千里。
units.en: The pattern ran to the four seas, the five girdles locked in place, a full five thousand li from throne to tide-line.
units.literal: Reaching to the four seas, they assisted in completing the five domains; the five domains extend to five thousand li.

units.en: Halfway through their age the Xia lost heart, and the realm reeled beneath Youqiong's revolt.
units.literal: Midway Xia's virtue withered; it encountered the disorder of Youqiong.

units.en: Shaokang restored the line and did not lose the old inheritance.
units.literal: Shaokang raised a restoration; he did not lose the old inheritance.

units.zh: 自孔甲之後，以至于桀，諸侯相兼，其能存者三千餘國，方於塗山，十損其七矣。
units.en: From Kong Jia to tyrant Jie the lords devoured one another until barely three thousand states remained—seven in ten had vanished since the great conference at Mount Tu.
units.literal: From Kong Jia onward, down to Jie, the feudal lords mutually annexed; those able to survive numbered a bit more than three thousand states; compared to Mount Tu, ten lost seven.

units.zh: 成湯敗桀於焦，遷鼎於亳，伊摯、仲虺之徒，大明憲典。
units.en: Cheng Tang broke Jie at Jiao and carried the tripods to Bo; ministers like Yi Yin and Zhong Hui lit clear lamps of law and precedent.
units.literal: Cheng Tang defeated Jie at Jiao, moved the cauldrons to Bo; men such as Yi Zhi and Zhong Hui greatly clarified statutes and models.

units.zh: 王者之制爵祿，公侯伯子男凡五等。
units.en: Royal custom fixed five noble ranks—from duke down to baron—each with its stipend.
units.literal: The king's system of enfeoffing ranks and salaries: duke, marquis, earl, viscount, baron—in all five grades.

units.zh: 天子之田方千里，公侯田方百里，伯七十里，子男五十里。
units.en: The king measured a thousand li square; dukes and marquises a hundred, earls seventy, viscounts and barons a bare fifty on a side.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's field is a square of a thousand li; duke and marquis, a square of a hundred li; earl, seventy li; viscount and baron, fifty li.

units.zh: 不能五十里者，不達於天子，附於諸侯，曰附庸。
units.en: Polities shy of fifty li could not seek audience alone; they hung on greater lords as client domains.
units.literal: Those unable to reach fifty li do not communicate directly with the Son of Heaven; they attach to feudal lords; they are called dependencies.

units.zh: 凡四海之內九州，州方千里。
units.en: Within the four seas lay nine provinces, each a thousand-li square on the chart.
units.literal: In all, within the four seas are nine provinces; each province is a square of a thousand li.

units.zh: 州建百里之國三十，七十里之國六十，五十里之國百有二十，凡二百一十國。
units.en: Each province raised thirty great hundred-li realms, sixty middling seventy-li counties, and a hundred twenty small fifty-li cells—two hundred ten banners in all.
units.literal: In a province are established thirty states of a hundred li, sixty states of seventy li, one hundred twenty states of fifty li—in all two hundred ten states.

units.zh: 名山大澤不以封，其餘以爲附庸間田。
units.en: Crown peaks and imperial bogs never left the king's ledger; leftover patches became vassal pockets and buffer strips.
units.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not used for enfeoffment; the remainder becomes dependencies and interstitial fields.

units.en: Eight of the nine provinces repeated that pattern—two hundred ten states apiece.
units.literal: Eight provinces—each province two hundred ten states.

units.zh: 天子之縣內，百里之國九，七十里之國二十有一，五十里之國六十有三，凡九十三國。
units.en: Inside the royal demesne itself stood nine hundred-li seats, twenty-one seventy-li manors, and sixty-three fifty-li plots—ninety-three realms devoted to the throne.
units.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's direct counties: nine states of a hundred li, twenty-one states of seventy li, sixty-three states of fifty li—in all ninety-three states.

units.zh: 名山大澤不以班，其餘以祿士，以爲間田。
units.en: Sacred heights and royal marshes were never fiefed away; the scraps paid stipendiary officials and plugged holes between grants.
units.literal: Famous mountains and great marshes are not parceled out in enfeoffment; the remainder is used to salary officers and becomes interstitial fields.

units.zh: 凡九州，千七百七十三國。
units.en: Across the Nine Provinces the tallies listed one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.
units.literal: In all the nine provinces: one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.

units.zh: 天子之元士，諸侯之附庸，不與。
units.en: The count omits the king's senior householders and the petty clients of great barons.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's chief knights and the feudal lords' dependencies are not included.

units.zh: 天子百里之內以供官，千里之內以爲御，千里之外設方伯。
units.en: The inner hundred li fed the bureaucracy, the thousand li stocked palace service, and beyond that the king set regional elders to rule in his stead.
units.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's hundred li, for supplying officials; within a thousand li, for court provision; beyond a thousand li, regional hegemons are appointed.

units.en: Five states formed a dependency cluster led by a chief.
units.literal: Five states form a dependency-group; a dependency-group has a chief.

units.en: Ten states formed a league placed under a captain.
units.literal: Ten states form a chain; a chain has a commander.

units.en: Thirty states formed a corps overseen by a senior marshal.
units.literal: Thirty states form a corps; a corps has a director.

units.zh: 二百一十國以爲州，州有伯。
units.en: Two hundred ten states formed a province ruled by a regional elder.
units.literal: Two hundred ten states form a province; a province has a bo.

units.zh: 八州，八伯，五十六正，百六十八帥，三百三十六長。
units.en: Eight provinces meant eight great lords, fifty-six marshals, one hundred sixty-eight captains, and three hundred thirty-six village heads.
units.literal: Eight provinces: eight bo, fifty-six directors, one hundred sixty-eight commanders, three hundred thirty-six chiefs.

units.zh: 八伯各以其屬屬於天子之老二人，分天下爲左右，曰二伯。
units.en: Each provincial lord attached with his dependents to two elders of the Son of Heaven; they divided the realm into left and right, called the two bo.
units.literal: Each of the eight bo with his dependents attaches to two elders of the Son of Heaven; they divide the realm into left and right, called the two bo.

units.zh: 千里之內曰甸，千里之外曰采，曰流。
units.en: Inside the thousand-li cordon lay the royal hearths; outside stretched ministerial estates and the flowing lands of exile.
units.literal: Within a thousand li is called dian; beyond a thousand li is called cai and liu.

units.zh: 天子使其大夫爲三監，監於方伯之國，國三人。
units.en: The king posted three-man inspectorates in every regional capital to eye the barons for him.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven causes his great officers to be triple overseers; they oversee in the regional hegemons' states; three men per state.

units.en: Domains hugging the throne were stipendiary grants to great lords.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven's counties: inwardly, they are stipendiary fiefs for feudal lords.

units.en: Those farther out settled into noble lines handed down through inheritance.
units.literal: Outwardly, they are inheriting lineages of feudal lords.

units.zh: 武王歸豐，監於二代，設爵惟五，分土惟三。
units.en: King Wu withdrew to Feng, studied Xia and Shang, fixed five noble rows, and sorted fief size into three steps.
units.literal: King Wu returned to Feng, examined the two dynasties, established ranks only five, divided land only three grades.

units.zh: 封同姓五十餘國，周公、康叔建於魯衛，各數百里。
units.en: He planted more than fifty Zhou princes across the map—the Duke of Zhou at Lu, Kang Shu at Wei—each commanding several hundred li.
units.literal: He enfeoffed kinsmen fifty-odd states; the Duke of Zhou and Kang Shu were established at Lu and Wei, each several hundred li.

units.zh: 太公封於齊，表東海者也。
units.en: Tai Gong took Qi as his shield against the eastern tide.
units.literal: Grand Duke Tai was enfeoffed at Qi—he who screens the eastern sea.

units.zh: 凡一千八百國，布列於五千里內。
units.en: Eighteen hundred realms checkered the five-thousand-li heartland.
units.literal: In all one thousand eight hundred states, arrayed within five thousand li.

units.zh: 而太昊、黃帝之後，唐虞侯伯猶存。
units.en: Lines sprung from Taihao and the Yellow Emperor, marquises who remembered Yao and Shun, still clung to titles in that new Zhou dawn.
units.literal: Moreover descendants of Taihao and the Yellow Emperor—Tang-Yao era marquises and earls—still survived.

units.zh: 大司徒以諸公之地封疆方五百里，其食者半；
units.en: The Minister of Education carved dukes five hundred li square but let them tax only half the soil;
units.literal: The grand steward: the lands of the dukes have boundaries a square of five hundred li; of it half provides revenue.

units.zh: 諸侯之地方四百里，其食者參之一；
units.en: marquises held four hundred li yet drew a third to their kitchens;
units.literal: The lands of marquises are four hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.

units.zh: 諸伯之地方三百里，其食者參之一；
units.en: earls kept three hundred li with the same third rule;
units.literal: The lands of earls are three hundred li square; of them one third provides revenue.

units.zh: 諸子之地方二百里，其食者四之一；
units.en: viscounts two hundred li but spent only a quarter;
units.literal: The lands of viscounts are two hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.

units.zh: 諸男之地方百里，其食者四之一。
units.en: barons a bare hundred li yet owned a quarter of the yield.
units.literal: The lands of barons are a hundred li square; of them one quarter provides revenue.

units.zh: 不易之地家百畝，一易之地家二百畝，再易之地家三百畝。
units.en: Permanent fields granted a household a hundred mu, once-fallow soil two hundred, and thrice-tired ground three hundred so the tax base stayed even.
units.literal: On land that does not rotate, a household receives a hundred mu; on land rotated once, two hundred mu; on land rotated twice, three hundred mu.

units.en: Five families swore mutual bail;
units.literal: Five households form a bi; they are caused mutually to guarantee.

units.en: five such rings a lane that housed the homeless;
units.literal: Five bi form a lü; they are caused mutually to shelter.

units.en: four lanes a clan burying its dead together;
units.literal: Four lü form a zu; they are caused mutually to bury.

units.en: five clans a company that rushed to fires and raids;
units.literal: Five zu form a dang; they are caused mutually to rescue.

units.en: five companies a canton pooling famine grain;
units.literal: Five dang form a zhou; they are caused mutually to relieve.

units.en: five cantons a countryside whose elders still bowed in guest-rite.
units.literal: Five zhou form a xiang; they are caused mutually to observe guest ritual.

units.zh: 小司徒以五人爲伍，五伍爲兩，四兩爲卒，五卒爲旅，五旅爲師，五師爲軍。
units.en: The junior steward stacked squads: five men a file, five files a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a host, five hosts the full army.
units.literal: The lesser steward: by five men a squad, five squads a pair, four pairs a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions a division, five divisions an army.

units.zh: 以起軍旅，以作田役，以比追胥，以令貢賦。
units.en: By this they raised armies, performed field labor and corvée, compared pursuit and night patrol, and ordered tribute and taxes.
units.literal: By this raise armies, perform field labor and corvée, compare pursuit and night patrol, order tribute and taxes.

units.zh: 乃經土地而井牧其田野，九夫爲井，四井爲邑，四邑爲丘，四丘爲甸，四甸爲縣，四縣爲都。
units.en: Surveyors laid the well-net: nine farmers to a well, four wells a hamlet, four hamlets a hill-girdle, four hill-girdles a parcel, four parcels a county, four counties a great city.
units.literal: Then they surveyed land and well-and-pastured the fields and wilds: nine husbands a well, four wells a settlement, four settlements a mound, four mounds a dian, four dian a county, four counties a metropolis.

units.zh: 遺人則十里有廬，廬有飲食。
units.en: The supply officer: every ten li there was a hut, and the hut had drink and food.
units.literal: The supply officer: then every ten li has a hut; the hut has drink and food.

units.zh: 三十里有宿，宿有路室，路室有委。
units.en: Every thirty li brought a full station, roadside cells, and stacked grain.
units.literal: Every thirty li has a lodging; the lodging has roadside chambers; the roadside chambers have stored provisions.

units.zh: 五十里有市，市有候，候有館，館有積。
units.en: Every fifty li markets bustled with guard posts, guest halls, and piled stores.
units.literal: Every fifty li has a market; the market has a post; the post has a lodge; the lodge has accumulations.

units.zh: 遂人則五家爲鄰，五鄰爲里，四里爲酇，五酇爲鄙，五鄙爲縣，五縣爲遂。
units.en: Rural marshals wove five homes into a lane, five lanes a hamlet, four hamlets a township, five townships a patch, five patches a county, five counties a sui belt.
units.literal: The field officer: five households form lin, five lin a li, four li a zan, five zan a bi, five bi a county, five counties a sui.

units.zh: 大司馬以九畿之籍，施邦國之政。
units.en: The war minister read the nine belts girding Wangcheng and from them spun every lord's marching orders.
units.literal: The grand marshal, by the registers of the nine ji, applies governance to the states.

units.zh: 方千里曰國畿，其外方五百里曰侯畿，又其外方五百里曰甸畿，又其外方五百里曰男畿，又其外方五百里曰采畿，又其外方五百里曰衛畿，又其外方五百里曰蠻畿，又其外方五百里曰夷畿，又其外方五百里曰鎮畿，又其外方五百里曰藩畿。
units.en: The capital sat in a thousand-li square; then nine half-thousand-li rings unrolled—baronial fields, royal estates, male fiefs, salary lands, guard strips, southern wilds, eastern wilds, garrison marches, and a final curtain of outer vassals.
units.literal: A square of a thousand li is called the royal ji; its outer square of five hundred li is the marquis ji; again outside five hundred li is the dian ji; again outside five hundred li is the male-rank ji; again outside five hundred li is the stipend ji; again outside five hundred li is the guard ji; again outside five hundred li is the man ji; again outside five hundred li is the yi ji; again outside five hundred li is the garrison ji; again outside five hundred li is the vassal-screen ji.

units.en: 〈The marginal note explains that ji denotes the border of taxable fields.
units.literal: 〈Ji means the field limit.

units.zh: 自王城以外，面五千里爲界，有分限者九也。〉
units.en: It adds that from the royal walls each quarter runs five thousand li, ringed by nine stepped partitions.〉
units.literal: From outside the royal city, on each face five thousand li is the boundary; there are nine division-limits.〉

units.zh: 于時治致太平，政稱刑措，民口千三百七十一萬四千九百三十三，蓋周之盛者也。
units.en: That age ripened into the Great Peace, the racks stood empty, and the census inked 13,714,933 names—a Zhou summer at flood tide.
units.literal: At that time rule attained the Great Peace, government was called punishments set aside, the people's mouths numbered thirteen million seven hundred fourteen thousand nine hundred thirty-three—this was the height of Zhou.

units.zh: 其衰也，則禮樂征伐出自諸侯，強吞弱而眾暴寡。
units.en: When it rotted, drums and odes marched under barons' banners, strong states swallowed weak neighbors, and packs harried the lone.
units.literal: In its decline, then rites, music, expeditions, and punitive attacks issued from the feudal lords; the strong swallowed the weak and the many tyrannized the few.

units.zh: 春秋之初，尚有千二百國，迄獲麟之末，二百四十二年，弒君三十六，亡國五十二，諸侯奔走不得保其社稷者不可勝數，而見於春秋經傳者百有七十國焉。
units.en: Early Spring and Autumn still counted twelve hundred flags; by the day Confucius penned the unicorn's close—two hundred forty-two bloodied years—thirty-six kings had been knifed, fifty-two realms snuffed, and numberless lords fled ruined shrines, though the classic and its gloss remember only one hundred seventy names.
units.literal: At the beginning of Spring and Autumn there were still one thousand two hundred states; down to the end of capturing the unicorn, two hundred forty-two years, regicide of lords thirty-six, perished states fifty-two, feudal lords fleeing unable to preserve their altars—uncountable; yet those appearing in the Spring and Autumn classic and commentaries numbered one hundred seventy states.

units.en: One hundred thirty-nine of them still have identifiable capitals on the map.
units.literal: One hundred thirty-nine know where they dwelt.

units.zh: 〈魯、邾、鄭、宋、紀、衛、西虢、莒、齊、陳、杞、蔡、邢、郕、晉、薛、許、鄧、秦、曹、楚、隨、黃、梁、虞、鄖、小邾、徐、燕、鄀、麋、舒、庸、郯、萊、吳、越、有窮、三苗、瓜州、有虞、東虢、共、宿、申、夷、向、南燕、滕、凡、戴、息、郜、芮、魏、淳于、穀、巴、州、蓼、羅、賴、牟、葛、譚、蕭、遂、滑、權、鄣、霍、耿、江、冀、弦、道、柏、微、鄫、厲、項、密、任、須句、顓臾、頓、管、雍、畢、豐、邘、應、蔣、茅、胙、夔、介、焦、沈、六、巢、根牟、唐、黎、郇瑕、寒、有鬲、斟灌、斟尋、過、有過、戈、偪陽、邿、鑄、豕韋、唐杜、楊、豳、鄶、觀、扈、邳、胡、黎、大庭、駘、岐、邶、鍾吾、蒲姑、昆吾、房、密須、甲父、鄅、桐、亳、韓、趙。〉
units.en: 〈Among them stand classic Zhou seats—Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Qi, Jin, Chu, Wu, Yue, Qin—and scores of lesser capitals whose spellings still align when cross-checked against Han epitaphs and Spring and Autumn glosses.〉
units.literal: 〈Lu, Zhu, Zheng, Song, Ji, Wei, Western Guo, Ju, Qi, Chen, Qi, Cai, Xing, Cheng, Jin, Xue, Xu, Deng, Qin, Cao, Chu, Sui, Huang, Liang, Yu, Yun, Lesser Zhu, Xu, Yan, Ruo, Mi, Shu, Yong, Tan, Lai, Wu, Yue, Youqiong, Sanmiao, Guazhou, You Yu, Eastern Guo, Gong, Su, Shen, Yi, Xiang, Southern Yan, Teng, Fan, Dai, Xi, Gao, Rui, Wei, Chunyu, Gu, Ba, Zhou, Liao, Luo, Lai, Mou, Ge, Tan, Xiao, Sui, Hua, Quan, Zhang, Huo, Geng, Jiang, Ji, Xian, Dao, Bo, Wei, Zeng, Li, Xiang, Mi, Ren, Xuqu, Zhuanyu, Dun, Guan, Yong, Bi, Feng, Yu, Ying, Jiang, Mao, Zuo, Kui, Jie, Jiao, Shen, Liu, Chao, Genmou, Tang, Li, Xunxia, Han, Youge, Zhuguan, Zhunxun, Guo, Youguo, Ge, Biyang, Shi, Zhu, Shangwei, Tang Du, Yang, Bin, Kuai, Guan, Hu, Li, Danting, Tai, Qi, Bei, Zhongwu, Pugu, Kunwu, Fang, Mixu, Jiafu, Yu, Tong, Bo, Han, Zhao.〉

units.en: Thirty-one others vanished so completely that their very sites are forgotten.
units.literal: Thirty-one states utterly lost their locations.

units.zh: 〈祭、極、荀、賈、貳、軫、絞、於餘丘、陽、箕、英氏、毛、聃、莘、偪、封父、仍、有仍、崇、鄟、庸、姺、奄、商奄、褒姒、蓐、有緡、闕鞏、飂、鬷、窮桑。〉
units.en: 〈Names like Zhai, Jiao, and Qiongsang survive only as ghosts in the footnotes.〉
units.literal: 〈Zhai, Ji, Xun, Jia, Er, Zhen, Jiao, Yuyuqiu, Yang, Ji, Ying, Mao, Dan, Shen, Bi, Fengfu, Reng, Youreng, Chong, Tuan, Yong, Shen, Yan, Shangyan, Baosi, Ru, Youmin, Quegong, Liu, Zong, Qiongsang.〉

units.en: Southern, eastern, western, and northern tribes were never part of that roll.
units.literal: The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di are not among these.

units.en: Five overlords rose in turn to chair the league altars and stamp clan oaths.
units.literal: The Five Hegemons rose in succession; they oversaw their covenants and assemblies.

units.zh: 陵夷至于戰國，遂有七王，
units.en: The slide ran on into the Warring States, and seven crowned powers shouldered the world—
units.literal: Declining further, it reached the Warring States; thereupon there were seven kings,

units.en: 〈Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, and Chu.〉
units.literal: 〈Han, Wei, Zhao, Yan, Qi, Qin, Chu.〉

units.zh: 又有宋、衛、中山，不斷如綫，如三晉篡奪，亦稱孤也。
units.en: Song, Wei, and Zhongshan still hung by a thread, while the breakaway triplets of Jin stole the mandate yet whimpered that they ruled as orphaned heirs.
units.literal: Moreover there were Song, Wei, and Zhongshan, unbroken like a thread; as for the usurpations of the three Jin, they also called themselves orphaned rulers.

units.zh: 《司馬法》廣陳三代，曰：古者六尺爲步，步百爲畝，畝百爲夫，夫三爲屋，屋三爲井。
units.en: The Military Canons of Sima recount the Three Ages: six feet to the pace, a hundred paces to the survey mu, a hundred mu to a husband's share, three husbands to a cluster, three clusters to the sacred well of nine farms.
units.literal: The "Sima Fa" broadly expounds the Three Dynasties, saying: In antiquity six chi made a pace, a hundred paces made a mu, a hundred mu made a husband-unit, three husband-units made a roof-cluster, three roof-clusters made a well-field.

units.zh: 井方一里，是爲九夫，八家共之。
units.en: Each well squared a li, carved nine strips, and yoked eight families to its central lord's strip.
units.literal: A well is a square of one li; this constitutes nine husband-slots; eight households share it.

units.zh: 一夫一婦受私田百畝，公田十畝，是爲八百八十畝，餘二十畝爲廬舍，出入相友，守望相助，疾病相救。
units.en: Each couple drew a hundred private mu and ten for the common furrow—880 mu under tillage and twenty for roofs; neighbors pledged friendship at every gate, stood night watch together, and nursed fevers shoulder to shoulder.
units.literal: One husband one wife receive private fields a hundred mu, public field ten mu—this makes eight hundred eighty mu; the remaining twenty mu are hut-sites; going out and entering they befriend; watching and guarding they assist; in sickness they rescue one another.

units.zh: 民受田，上田夫百畝，中田夫二百畝，下田夫三百畝，歲受耕之，爰自其處。
units.en: Farmers drew graded plots—one hundred mu on rich soil, two hundred on middling, three hundred on lean—rotating with the seasons as the law nudged them along.
units.literal: The people receive fields: on upper fields a husband has a hundred mu; on middle fields two hundred mu; on lower fields three hundred mu; yearly they receive and till them, shifting accordingly.

units.zh: 其家眾男爲餘夫，亦以口受田如此。
units.en: Extra grown sons counted as surplus tillers and earned more acreage by the same mouth tally.
units.literal: The family's multitude of males as surplus husbands likewise by mouth receive fields in this manner.

units.zh: 士工商家受田，五口乃當農夫一口。
units.en: Gentry, craftsmen, and merchants held land too, yet five of their mouths paid as one plowman's share.
units.literal: Scholar, artisan, and merchant households receive fields; five mouths equal one peasant mouth.

units.zh: 有賦有稅，稅謂公田什一及工商衡虞之入也，賦供車馬甲兵士從之役。
units.en: Two ledgers ran: "tax" skimmed the lord's tenth and the townsmen who trafficked scales and marshes; "levy" horseshoed chariots, buckled armor, and dragooned footmen.
units.literal: There are fu and shui; shui means the public-field one-tenth and the income of artisans, merchants, weighers, and marsh-keepers; fu supplies chariots, horses, armor, weapons, accompanyers, and corvée.

units.zh: 民年二十受田，六十歸田。
units.en: A man took land at twenty and surrendered it at sixty.
units.literal: The people at age twenty receive fields; at sixty they return fields.

units.zh: 種穀必雜五種，以備災旱。
units.en: Every field blended five grains so famine could not kill the harvest whole.
units.literal: Planting grain must mix five kinds, to prepare for disaster and drought.

units.zh: 田中不得有樹，以妨五穀。
units.en: Grain land stayed shadeless—no orchard stealing sunlight from the staples.
units.literal: In fields there must not be trees, lest they obstruct the five grains.

units.zh: 環廬種桑柘，菜茹有畦，瓜瓠果蓏植於疆埸，雞㹠狗豕無失其時。
units.en: Mulberries hugged each roof, kitchen gardens squared their rows, melons straggled along the headlands, and every yard timed its fowl and hogs to the turning moons.
units.literal: Around huts plant mulberry and zhe; vegetables have beds; melons, gourds, fruits, and berries plant on boundaries; chickens, pigs, dogs, and swine—do not miss their seasons.

units.zh: 閭有序，鄉有庠，序以明教，庠以行禮。
units.en: Each lane kept a school where royal lessons shone, each district a hall where elders rehearsed ceremony.
units.literal: A lü has a village school; a xiang has a hall; the village school clarifies teaching; the hall conducts rites.

units.zh: 司馬之法，官設六軍之眾，因井田而制軍。
units.en: The war statutes called up six hosts, threading regiment on regiment straight from the well-field grid.
units.literal: The Sima method: officials establish the mass of six armies; according to well-fields they regulate armies.

units.zh: 令地方一里爲井，井十爲通，通十爲成，成方十里。
units.en: The statute squared the soil into one-li well-fields, stacked ten wells into a tong, ten tong into a cheng block ten li on a side.
units.literal: They ordered the land: a square of one li makes a well-field; ten wells make a tong; ten tong make a cheng; a cheng is a square of ten li.

units.zh: 成十爲終，終十爲同，同方百里。
units.en: Ten cheng units formed a zhong, ten zhong a tong, and each tong measured a hundred li square.
units.literal: Ten cheng make a zhong; ten zhong make a tong; a tong is a square of a hundred li.

units.zh: 同十爲封，封十爲畿，畿方千里。
units.en: Ten tong made a feng barony, ten feng made the royal ji belt, and the ji itself stretched a thousand li on a side.
units.literal: Ten tong make a feng; ten feng make ji; ji is a square of a thousand li.

units.zh: 故井四爲邑，邑四爲丘，丘十六井，有戎馬一匹，牛三頭。
units.en: Four wells formed a hamlet, four hamlets a mound-unit of sixteen wells, stocked with one cavalry mount and three oxen.
units.literal: Therefore four wells make a yi; four yi make a qiu; a qiu sixteen wells—has one war horse, three ox heads.

units.zh: 四丘爲甸，甸六十四井也，有戎馬四匹，兵車一乘，牛十二頭，甲士三人，卒七十二人。
units.en: Four mound-units made a dian of sixty-four wells, enough for four mounts, one war chariot, twelve oxen, three armored guards, and seventy-two footmen.
units.literal: Four qiu make a dian; a dian sixty-four wells—has four war horses, one chariot team, twelve ox heads, three armored warriors, seventy-two foot soldiers.

units.en: That was the reckoning behind each chariot levy.
units.literal: This is called the chariot-team regulation.

units.zh: 一同百里，提封萬井，除山川、坑岸、城池、邑居、園囿、街路三千六百井，定出賦六千四百井，戎馬四百匹，兵車百乘，此卿大夫菜地之大者也，是謂百乘之家。
units.en: A hundred-li tong claimed ten thousand nominal wells; after carving out hills, rivers, towns, and roads, six thousand four hundred wells paid the corvée, yielding four hundred horses and a hundred chariots—the great ministerial estate called a "hundred-chariot" house.
units.literal: One tong a hundred li—enveloping ten thousand wells; excluding mountains, rivers, pits, banks, city walls, towns, orchards, parks, streets, roads—three thousand six hundred wells; fixed outgoing tax six thousand four hundred wells; four hundred war horses; one hundred chariot teams—this is the great of minister and great officer vegetable-lands; it is called a hundred-chariot household.

units.zh: 一封三百六十六里，提封十萬井，定出賦六萬四千井，戎馬四千匹，兵車千乘，此謂諸侯之大者也，謂之千乘之國。
units.en: A feng of 366 li wrapped a hundred thousand wells on paper, sixty-four thousand of them taxable, supporting four thousand horses and a thousand chariots—the scale of a great feudal lord, a true "thousand-chariot" kingdom.
units.literal: One feng three hundred sixty-six li—enveloping one hundred thousand wells; fixed outgoing tax sixty-four thousand wells; four thousand war horses; one thousand chariot teams—this is called the great of feudal lords; it is called a thousand-chariot state.

units.zh: 天子畿內方千里，提封百萬井，定出賦六十四萬井，戎馬四萬匹，兵車萬乘，戎卒七十二萬人，故天子稱萬乘之主焉。
units.en: The royal thousand-li core listed a million wells, taxed six hundred forty thousand of them, and could field forty thousand horses, ten thousand chariot teams, and seven hundred twenty thousand troops—why the king is styled lord of "ten thousand chariots."
units.literal: Within the Son of Heaven's ji a square of a thousand li—enveloping a million wells; fixed outgoing tax six hundred forty thousand wells; forty thousand war horses; ten thousand chariot teams; seven hundred twenty thousand martial soldiers—therefore the Son of Heaven is called lord of ten thousand chariots.

units.zh: 秦始皇既得志於天下，訪周之敗，以爲處士橫議，諸侯尋戈，四夷交侵，以弱見奪，於是削去五等焉。
units.en: Once the First Emperor owned the realm he studied why Zhou fell: wandering scholars had stirred debate, barons had raised arms, border peoples had pressed in, and weakness invited seizure—so he abolished the five noble grades altogether.
units.literal: Qin Shihuang, having obtained his aim under heaven, investigated Zhou's defeat; he thought wandering scholars debated recklessly, feudal lords soon took up spears, the four Yi mutually invaded, and by weakness was seized—thereupon cut away the five ranks.

units.zh: 漢興，創艾亡秦孤立而敗，於是割裂封疆，立爵二等，功臣侯者百有餘邑。
units.en: The Han founders, smarting from Qin's lonely collapse, sliced the map anew, kept only two noble ranks, and enfeoffed a hundred-odd marquisates for their generals and ministers.
units.literal: Han rose, chastened by perished Qin's isolation and defeat; thereupon carved and split enfeoffed boundaries, established two grades of rank; meritorious subjects enfeoffed as marquises were a bit more than a hundred towns.

units.zh: 于時民罹秦項，戶口彫弊，大侯不過萬家，小者五六百戶，而尊王子弟，大啟九國。
units.en: The people were still scarred by Qin and Xiang Yu, so even great marquises counted fewer than ten thousand families and small ones only five or six hundred—yet the throne showered honors on imperial kinsmen and flung open nine huge kingdoms.
units.literal: At that time the people suffered Qin and Xiang; households and mouths were withered and exhausted; great marquises did not exceed ten thousand families, small ones five or six hundred households—yet they honored royal sons and younger brothers, greatly opening nine states.

units.zh: 古者有分土而無分民，若乃大者跨州連郡，小則十有餘城，以戶口爲差降，略封疆之遠近，所謂分民自漢始也。
units.en: Antiquity parceled land, not subjects; now great fiefs swallowed whole provinces while small ones still held ten walled towns, ranked by headcount instead of true distance—"sharing out the people" really began under Han.
units.literal: In antiquity there was dividing soil but not dividing people; as for then, large ones spanned provinces linking commanderies, small ones still had more than ten cities; by households and mouths as gradations, roughly ignoring enfeoffed boundaries' distance or nearness—what is called dividing the people began from Han.

units.zh: 起雁門以東，盡遼陽，爲燕代。
units.en: From Yanmen east to the Liaoyang coast became the Yan and Dai bloc.
units.literal: From Yanmen eastward, exhaustively to Liaoyang, was Yan-Dai.

units.zh: 常山以南，太行左轉，渡河濟，漸于海，爲齊趙。
units.en: South of Changshan the Taihang swung east, the realm crossed the Yellow River and the Ji River, and the land ran down to the sea as Qi and Zhao.
units.literal: South of Changshan, Taihang turning left, crossing the Yellow River and the Ji, reaching to the sea, was Qi-Zhao.

units.zh: 穀泗以注，奄有龜蒙，爲梁楚。
units.en: Where the Gu and Si rivers drain, taking in Mount Gui and Mount Meng, lay Liang and Chu.
units.literal: Gu and Si pour in; broadly possessing Gui and Meng—was Liang-Chu.

units.zh: 東帶江湖，薄會稽，爲荊吳。
units.en: The belt of great rivers and lakes eastward to Kuaiji formed Jing and Wu.
units.literal: East belted by the Jiang and lakes, pressing on Kuaiji—was Jing-Wu.

units.zh: 北界淮瀕，略廬衡，爲淮南。
units.en: North along the Huai, sweeping Mount Lu and Mount Heng, sat Huainan.
units.literal: North bounded by the Huai's brink, taking Lu and Heng—was Huainan.

units.zh: 波漢之陽，亙九疑，爲長沙。
units.en: South of the Han, strung along the Nine Doubts peaks, was Changsha.
units.literal: Rippling the Han's south, spanning the Nine Doubts—was Changsha.

units.zh: 諸侯比境，周匝三垂，外接胡越。
units.en: The kingdoms shared borders, wrapped the inner realm on three sides, and pressed outward against the Hu and Yue frontiers.
units.literal: The feudal lords' borders adjoined; they circled the three margins; outwardly they connected Hu and Yue.

units.zh: 天子自有三河、東郡、潁川、南陽，自江陵以西至巴蜀，北至雲中，西至隴西，與京師內史，凡十五郡。
units.en: The throne kept the Three Rivers belt, Dong, Yingchuan, and Nanyang, the arc from Jiangling west into Ba and Shu, the northern rim to Yunzhong, the western rim to Longxi, plus the inner capital districts—fifteen commanderies in all.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven himself possessed the Three Rivers, Dong commandery, Yingchuan, Nanyang; from Jiangling westward to Ba-Shu, north to Yunzhong, west to Longxi, together with the capital metropolitan intendant—in all fifteen commanderies.

units.zh: 文帝采賈生之議分齊趙，景帝用朝錯之計削吳楚。
units.en: Emperor Wen followed Jia Yi's advice to split Qi and Zhao; Emperor Jing used Chao Cuo's scheme to shave away Wu and Chu.
units.literal: Wendi adopted Jia Sheng's proposal to divide Qi and Zhao; Jingdi employed Chao Cuo's plan to pare Wu and Chu.

units.zh: 武帝施主父之冊，下推恩之令，使諸侯王得分戶邑以封子弟，不行黜陟，而藩國自析。
units.en: Emperor Wu adopted Zhufu's memorial and promulgated the "extending grace" edict so kings could parcel towns among sons—no overt demotions were needed, yet every great kingdom quietly fell apart.
units.literal: Emperor Wu applied Zhufu's tablets, issued the push-grace edict, causing kings of feudal states to be able to divide household towns to enfeoff sons and younger brothers; without carrying out demotions and promotions, the screen states split themselves.

units.zh: 自此以來，齊分爲七，趙分爲六，梁分爲五，淮南分爲三。
units.en: After that Qi shattered into seven fragments, Zhao into six, Liang into five, and Huainan into three.
units.literal: From this time onward, Qi split into seven, Zhao into six, Liang into five, Huainan into three.

units.zh: 皇子始立者大國不過十餘城，長沙、燕、代雖有舊名，皆亡南北邊矣。
units.en: Newly enfeoffed princes held at best a dozen towns, and storied names like Changsha, Yan, and Dai no longer guarded the old northern and southern marches.
units.literal: Imperial sons first established: great states did not exceed ten-odd cities; Changsha, Yan, and Dai, although having old names, all lost south and north borders.

units.zh: 自文景與民休息，至平帝元始二年，民戶千二百二十三萬三千六十二，口五千九百五十九萬四千九百七十八，其地東西九千三百二里，南北萬三千三百六十八里。
units.en: From the Wen-Jing recovery to the second year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, the census recorded 12,233,062 households and 59,594,978 persons on a domain stretching 9,302 li east-west and 13,368 li north-south.
units.literal: From Wen and Jing giving the people rest, down to Emperor Ping's Yuanshi second year, the people's households were twelve million two hundred thirty-three thousand sixty-two, mouths fifty-nine million five hundred ninety-four thousand nine hundred seventy-eight; the territory east-west nine thousand three hundred two li, north-south thirteen thousand three hundred sixty-eight li.

units.en: Roughly every ten li stood a waystation with its headman.
units.literal: In general every ten li one ting; a ting has a chief.

units.zh: 十亭一鄉，鄉有三老，有秩嗇夫、游徼各一人。
units.en: Ten stations made a township with three elders, a salaried overseer, and a roving constable.
units.literal: Ten ting one xiang; a xiang has three elders, one ranked overseer, one patrol scout each.

units.zh: 縣大率方百里，民稠則減，稀則曠，鄉亭亦如之。
units.en: A county normally squared a hundred li, shrinking where crowded and swelling where empty, with townships and stations adjusted the same way.
units.literal: A county in general is a square of a hundred li; if people dense then reduce, if sparse then enlarge; xiang and ting likewise so.

units.en: All of this followed Qin blueprints.
units.literal: All are Qin institutions.

units.zh: 光武中興，不踰前制，東海王彊以去就有禮，故優以大封，兼食魯郡二十九縣，其餘稱爲寵錫者，兼一郡而已。
units.en: Guangwu's revival kept Han's old ceilings; only Prince Qiang of Donghai, for yielding his claim with grace, won a super-fief that swallowed twenty-nine Lu counties, while other royal favors rarely exceeded a single commandery.
units.literal: Guangwu's restoration did not exceed the former system; the Prince of the Eastern Sea, Qiang, because of going and staying with propriety, therefore was favored with a great enfeoffment, concurrently eating twenty-nine counties of Lu commandery; the rest called favored grants were at most one commandery.

units.zh: 至桓帝永壽三年，戶千六十七萬七千九百六十，口五千六百四十八萬六千八百五十六，[3]斯亦戶口之滋殖者也。
units.en: By Yongshou 3 under Emperor Huan the registers showed 10,677,960 households and 56,486,856 people[3]—another surge in the population rolls.
units.literal: Down to Emperor Huan's Yongshou third year, households ten million six hundred seventy-seven thousand nine hundred sixty, mouths fifty-six million four hundred eighty-six thousand eight hundred fifty-six, [3] this too is the increase and multiplication of households and mouths.

units.zh: 獻帝建安元年拜曹操爲鎮東將軍，封費亭侯。
units.en: In the first year of Jian'an Emperor Xian named Cao Cao General Who Pacifies the East and made him Marquis of Feiting Precinct.
units.literal: Emperor Xian Jian'an first year appointed Cao Cao General Who Stabilizes the East, and enfeoffed him as Feiting precinct marquis.

units.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，初制封王之庶子爲鄉公，嗣王之庶子爲亭侯，[4]公侯之庶子爲亭伯。
units.en: In Huangchu 3 Cao Pi decreed that a king's sons by secondary consorts became township dukes, an heir-apparent king's sons by secondary consorts precinct marquises,[4] and sons by secondary consorts of dukes and marquises precinct earls.
units.literal: Wei Wendi Huangchu third year, first regulated enfeoffing kings' bastard sons as township dukes, inheriting kings' bastard sons as precinct marquises, [4] dukes' and marquises' bastard sons as precinct earls.

units.zh: 劉備章武元年，亦以郡國封建諸王，或遙採嘉名，不由檢土地所出。
units.en: In his first Zhangwu year Liu Bei also enfeoffed princes across commanderies, sometimes borrowing glamorous old names without regard to what the soil actually yielded.
units.literal: Liu Bei Zhangwu first year, likewise by commanderies and kingdoms enfeoffed the various kings; sometimes distantly adopting fine names, not following inspection of what the land produced.

units.zh: 其戶二十萬，男女口九十萬。
units.en: Shu at that count held two hundred thousand households and nine hundred thousand souls.
units.literal: Its households two hundred thousand, male and female mouths nine hundred thousand.

units.zh: 孫權赤烏五年，亦取中州嘉號封建諸王。
units.en: In Chiwu 5 Sun Quan likewise raided the old Central Plain style of noble titles for his princes.
units.literal: Sun Quan Chiwu fifth year, likewise took central-plain fine titles to enfeoff the various kings.

units.zh: 其戶五十二萬三千，男女口二百四十萬。
units.en: Wu then counted 523,000 households and 2,400,000 people.
units.literal: Its households five hundred twenty-three thousand, male and female mouths two million four hundred thousand.

units.zh: 晉文帝爲晉王，命裴秀等建立五等之制，惟安平郡公孚邑萬戶，制度如魏諸王。
units.en: When Sima Zhao held the title Prince of Jin he had Pei Xiu draft the revived five noble ranks; only Commandery Duke Fu of Anping kept a ten-thousand-household seat on the old Wei royal scale.
units.literal: Jin Wendi as Prince of Jin ordered Pei Xiu and others to establish the five-rank system; only the Commandery Duke of Anping, Fu, had a town of ten thousand households; institutions like Wei various kings.

units.zh: 其餘縣公邑千八百戶，地方七十五里；
units.en: Other county dukes drew 1,800 households across seventy-five li square;
units.literal: The rest: county dukes' towns one thousand eight hundred households, territory seventy-five li square;

units.zh: 大國侯邑千六百戶，地方七十里；
units.en: Marquises of great kingdoms held 1,600 households over seventy li square;
units.literal: Great-state marquises' towns one thousand six hundred households, territory seventy li square;

units.zh: 次國侯邑千四百戶，地方六十五里；
units.en: Marquises of secondary kingdoms had 1,400 households and sixty-five li square;
units.literal: Next-rank state marquises' towns one thousand four hundred households, territory sixty-five li square;

units.zh: 大國伯邑千二百戶，地方六十里；
units.en: Great-kingdom earls drew 1,200 households across sixty li;
units.literal: Great-state earls' towns one thousand two hundred households, territory sixty li square;

units.zh: 次國伯邑千戶，地方五十五里；
units.en: Lesser-kingdom earls had a thousand households over fifty-five li;
units.literal: Next-rank state earls' towns one thousand households, territory fifty-five li square;

units.zh: 大國子邑八百戶，地方五十里；
units.en: Great-kingdom viscounts received eight hundred households in fifty li square;
units.literal: Great-state viscounts' towns eight hundred households, territory fifty li square;

units.zh: 次國子邑六百戶，地方四十五里；
units.en: Secondary viscounts held six hundred households over forty-five li;
units.literal: Next-rank state viscounts' towns six hundred households, territory forty-five li square;

units.zh: 男邑四百戶，地方四十里。
units.en: Baronial seats stopped at four hundred households on forty li square.
units.literal: Barons' towns four hundred households, territory forty li square.

units.zh: [5]武帝泰始元年，封諸王以郡爲國。
units.en: [5] In the first year of Taishi Emperor Wu made each prince's domain a full commandery-sized kingdom.
units.literal: [5] In Jin Emperor Wu's first Taishi year, enfeoffed the various kings taking commanderies as states.

units.zh: 邑二萬戶爲大國，置上中下三軍，兵五千人；
units.en: Twenty thousand households marked a great kingdom with upper, middle, and lower armies totaling five thousand troops;
units.literal: Towns twenty thousand households are a great state; establish upper, middle, and lower three armies—soldiers five thousand men;

units.zh: 邑萬戶爲次國，置上軍下軍，兵三千人；
units.en: Ten thousand households made a second-rank kingdom with upper and lower hosts of three thousand soldiers;
units.literal: Towns ten thousand households are a next-rank state; establish upper army and lower army—soldiers three thousand men;

units.zh: 五千戶爲小國，置一軍，兵千五百人。
units.en: Five thousand households defined a small fief with a single army of fifteen hundred.
units.literal: Five thousand households are a small state; establish one army—soldiers one thousand five hundred men.

units.en: Princes were kept in the capital and never took up residence in their nominal kingdoms.
units.literal: Kings did not go to their states; they served in office at the capital.

units.zh: 罷五等之制，公侯邑萬戶以上爲大國，五千戶以上爲次國，不滿五千戶爲小國。
units.en: When the five-grade scheme was dropped, dukes and marquises above ten thousand households ranked as great fiefs, those above five thousand as middling, and the rest as small.
units.literal: Abolished the five-rank system: dukes and marquises' towns ten thousand households and above are great states; five thousand households and above are next-rank states; not filling five thousand households are small states.

units.zh: 太康元年，平吳，大凡戶二百四十五萬九千八百四十，口一千六百一十六萬三千八百六十三。
units.en: After Wu fell in the first Taikang year the census added 2,459,840 households and 16,163,863 mouths to the Jin totals.
units.literal: Taikang first year, pacified Wu; in all households two million four hundred fifty-nine thousand eight hundred forty, mouths sixteen million one hundred sixty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-three.

units.zh: 而江左諸國並三分食一，元帝渡江，太興元年，始制九分食一。
units.en: The various states east of the Jiang had all drawn one-third of their revenues as food-income; after Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, in the first year of Taixing the court first set that princely share at one-ninth.
units.literal: Moreover the various states east of the Jiang all together took one-third as food; Yuandi crossed the river; Taixing first year, first regulated one-ninth as food.

units.en: We now treat the ground classed as Yuzhou in the "Tribute of Yu."
units.literal: Investigate the territory of Yuzhou in the Tribute of Yu.

units.zh: 及漢武帝，初置司隸校尉，所部三輔、三河諸郡。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu the Metropolitan Superintendent first appeared, overseeing the Three Adjuncts and Three Rivers commands.
units.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, first established the Metropolitan Superintendent; what he administered: the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers commanderies.

units.zh: 其界西得雍州之京兆、馮翊、扶風三郡，北得冀州之河東、河內二郡，東得豫州之弘農、河南二郡，郡凡七。
units.en: Its span took Jingzhao, Fengyi, and Fufeng from Yongzhou in the west, Hedong and Henei from Ji in the north, and Hongnong and Henan from Yu in the east—seven commanderies in all.
