units.literal: Its boundary: west obtained Yongzhou's Jingzhao, Fengyi, Fufeng three commanderies; north obtained Jizhou's Hedong, Henei two commanderies; east obtained Yuzhou's Hongnong, Henan two commanderies—commanderies in all seven.

units.zh: 位望隆于牧伯，[6]銀印青綬。
units.en: The post outranked provincial governors,[6] bearing a silver seal on green ribbon.
units.literal: Position and outlook loftier than shepherds and regional lords, [6] silver seal, green ribbon.

units.zh: 及光武都洛陽，司隸所部與前漢不異。
units.en: When Guangwu moved the capital to Luoyang the metropolitan belt matched Western Han's layout.
units.literal: Reaching Guangwu's capital at Luoyang, what the Metropolitan Superintendent administered did not differ from Former Han.

units.zh: 魏氏受禪，即都漢宮，司隸所部河南、河東、河內、弘農并冀州之平陽，合五郡，置司州。
units.en: Wei took the Han palaces at Luoyang, folded Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, and Pingyang from Ji into one metropolitan zone, and renamed it Sizhou.
units.literal: The Wei house received abdication, immediately capital at Han palaces; what the Metropolitan Superintendent administered: Henan, Hedong, Henei, Hongnong, together with Jizhou's Pingyang—combined five commanderies, established Sizhou.

units.zh: 晉仍居魏都，乃以三輔還屬雍州，分河南立滎陽，分雍州之京兆立上洛，廢東郡立頓丘，遂定名司州，以司隸校尉統之。
units.en: Jin stayed in Wei's Luoyang, sent the Three Adjuncts back to Yongzhou, peeled Yingyang from Henan and Shangluo from Jingzhao, replaced Dong with Dunqiu, and locked in the name Sizhou under the metropolitan commandant.
units.literal: Jin still dwelt at Wei's capital; thereupon returned the Three Adjuncts to Yongzhou, split Henan to establish Yingyang, split Yongzhou's Jingzhao to establish Shangluo, abolished Dong commandery to establish Dunqiu, thereupon fixed the name Sizhou, with the Metropolitan Superintendent governing it.

units.zh: 州統郡一十二，縣一百，戶四十七萬五千七百。
units.en: Sizhou ruled twelve commanderies and a hundred counties with 475,700 registered households.
units.literal: The province commands twelve commanderies, one hundred counties, households four hundred seventy-five thousand seven hundred.

units.en: [7] This marks editorial footnote seven in the source apparatus.
units.literal: [7] Editorial footnote marker seven.

units.literal: Henan commandery

units.en: 〈First set up under Han.
units.literal: 〈Established in Han.

units.zh: 統縣十二，戶一十一萬四千四百。
units.en: It governed twelve counties and 111,400 households.
units.literal: Commands twelve counties, households one hundred eleven thousand four hundred.

units.en: Its capital seat held a metropolitan yin governor.〉
units.literal: Establishes a yin governor.〉

units.en: Luoyang
units.literal: Luoyang

units.en: 〈The county had a captain of police.
units.literal: 〈Establishes a county captain of police.

units.en: The city was divided into five wards and three market wards.
units.literal: Five wards, three markets.

units.en: Its wall ran seven li east-west and nine li north-south.
units.literal: East-west seven li, north-south nine li.

units.zh: 東有建春、東陽、清明三門，南有開陽、平昌、宣陽、建陽四門，西有廣陽、西明、閶闔三門，北有大夏、廣莫二門。
units.en: East wall opened Jianchun, Dongyang, and Qingming; the south four gates including Kaiyang; the west Guangyang, Ximing, and Changhe; the north Daxia and Guangmo.
units.literal: East has three gates: Jianchun, Dongyang, Qingming; south has four gates: Kaiyang, Pingchang, Xuanyang, Jianyang; west has three gates: Guangyang, Ximing, Changhe; north has two gates: Daxia, Guangmo.

units.zh: 司隸校尉、河南尹及百官列城內也。〉
units.en: The metropolitan commandant, the Henan governor, and the full bureaucracy sat inside those walls.〉
units.literal: The Metropolitan Superintendent, Henan governor, and the hundred officials are arrayed within the city.〉

units.en: Henan county
units.literal: Henan

units.en: 〈The Eastern Zhou royal city at Jia-Ru.〉
units.literal: 〈Zhou eastern capital royal city Jia-Ru.〉

units.literal: Gong

units.zh: 〈周孝王封周桓公孫惠公於鞏，號東周，故戰國時有東、西周號。
units.en: 〈King Xiao enfeoffed Duke Hui of Zhou at Gong as "Eastern Zhou," which is why Warring States texts speak of eastern and western Zhou polities.
units.literal: 〈King Xiao of Zhou enfeoffed Duke Hui of Zhou, grandson of Duke Huan of Zhou, at Gong, titled Eastern Zhou; therefore in Warring States times there were Eastern and Western Zhou titles.

units.en: Mount Mang and Shouyang marked its frontier.〉
units.literal: Mount Mang and Shouyang are its boundary.〉

units.en: The entries Heyin and Xin'an lay along this stretch.
units.literal: Heyin, Xin'an

units.en: 〈The seat of Hangu Pass.〉
units.literal: 〈Where Hangu Pass is located.〉

units.literal: Chenggao

units.en: 〈Held the barrier known in Zheng times as Wulao.〉
units.literal: 〈Has a pass—Zheng's Wulao.〉

units.en: Goushi county
units.literal: Goushi

units.en: 〈Contained the Liu settlement, seat of the Zhou minister styled Liu Zi.
units.literal: 〈Has Liu cluster—the town of Zhou great officer Liu Zi.

units.en: It also held Yanshou town and the shrine to the immortals.〉
units.literal: Has Yanshou city, immortal shrine.〉

units.zh: 是時遺黎南渡，元帝僑置兗州，寄居京口。
units.en: Survivors forded the Yangzi, and Yuan of Jin papered a migrant Yanzhou onto Jingkou.
units.literal: At that time surviving commoners crossed south; Yuandi sojourning established Yanzhou, lodging at Jingkou.

units.zh: 明帝以郗鑒爲刺史，寄居廣陵，置濮陽、濟陰、高平、太山等郡。
units.en: Emperor Ming appointed Xi Jian as regional inspector with a seat at Guangling, attaching Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and more nominal commanderies to him.
units.literal: Mingdi made Xi Jian inspector, lodging at Guangling, establishing Puyang, Jiyin, Gaoping, Taishan, and other commanderies.

units.zh: 後改爲南兗州，或還江南，或居盱眙，或居山陽。
units.en: The office was rebranded South Yanzhou and drifted between Jiangnan, Xuyi, and Shanyang as the front moved.
units.literal: Later changed to South Yanzhou, sometimes returned south of the river, sometimes dwelt at Xuyi, sometimes dwelt at Shanyang.

units.zh: 後始割地爲境，常居廣陵，南與京口對岸。
units.en: Eventually real soil was assigned and the seat settled at Guangling, opposite Jingkou on the far shore.
units.literal: Later they began to cut land as borders, constantly dwelt at Guangling, south facing Jingkou across the bank.

units.zh: 咸康四年，於北譙界立陳留郡。
units.en: Xiankang four saw a new Chenliu commandery planted along the northern Qiao frontier.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang, on the border of northern Qiao they established Chenliu commandery.

units.zh: 安帝分廣陵郡之建陵、臨江、如皋、寧海、蒲濤五縣置山陽郡，屬南兗州。
units.en: Emperor An carved five Guangling bayside counties into a Shanyang commandery still listed under South Yanzhou.
units.literal: Emperor An split off Jianling, Linjiang, Rugao, Ninghai, and Putao counties from Guangling commandery to establish Shanyang commandery, belonging to South Yanzhou.

units.en: The Tribute of Yu maps this belt between the Jing range and the Yellow River.
units.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, it is the land between Jing and the river.

units.en: The Rites of Zhou names the tract south of the river Yuzhou.'
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou: "South of the river is called Yuzhou."

units.zh: 豫者舒也，言稟中和之氣，性理安舒也。
units.en: Yu' implies ease, because the land drinks in balanced vapors and its temper stays unruffled.
units.literal: Yu means ease; saying it receives the harmonious qi, nature and pattern are calm and easeful.

units.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「鉤鈐星別爲豫州。」
units.en: The Yuanming Bao pairs the Gou-Qian asterisms with Yuzhou.'
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says: "The Gou and Qian stars separately become Yuzhou."

units.zh: 地界，西自華山，東至于淮，北自濟，南界荊山。
units.en: Its compass ran from Mount Hua westward to the Huai eastward, from the Ji northward to Mount Jing southward.
units.literal: Its boundaries: west from Mount Hua, east reaching to the Huai, north from the Ji, south bounded by Mount Jing.

units.zh: 秦兼天下，以爲三川、河東、南陽、潁川、碭、泗水、薛七郡。
units.en: Qin's first map folded the region into Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue commanderies.
units.literal: Qin united all under heaven, making seven commanderies: Sanchuan, Hedong, Nanyang, Yingchuan, Dang, Sishui, and Xue.

units.zh: 漢改三川爲河南郡，武帝置十三州，豫州舊名不改，以河南、河東二郡屬司隸，又以南陽屬荊州。
units.en: Han retitled Sanchuan Henan, Emperor Wu's thirteen circuits kept the Yuzhou label, while Henan and Hedong answered to Sili and Nanyang slid under Jingzhou.
units.literal: Han changed Sanchuan to Henan commandery; Emperor Wu established thirteen provinces; the old name of Yuzhou was not changed, taking Henan and Hedong two commanderies as belonging to Sili, and further taking Nanyang as belonging to Jingzhou.

units.zh: 先是，改泗水曰沛郡，改碭郡曰梁，改薛曰魯，分梁沛立汝南郡，分潁川立淮陽郡。
units.en: Earlier rounds had renamed Sishui to Pei, Dang to Liang, Xue to Lu, spun Runan from Liang and Pei, and Huaiyang from Yingchuan.
units.literal: Before this, changed Sishui to Pei commandery, changed Dang commandery to Liang, changed Xue to Lu, split Liang and Pei to establish Runan commandery, split Yingchuan to establish Huaiyang commandery.

units.zh: 後漢章帝改淮陽曰陳郡。
units.en: Eastern Han's Emperor Zhang rechristened Huaiyang Chen.
units.literal: Later Han Emperor Zhang changed Huaiyang to Chen commandery.

units.zh: 魏武分沛立譙郡，魏文分汝南立弋陽郡。
units.en: Cao Cao carved Qiao from Pei, and Cao Pi raised Yiyang from Runan.
units.literal: Wei Wu split Pei to establish Qiao commandery; Wei Wen split Runan to establish Yiyang commandery.

units.zh: 及武帝受命，又分潁川立襄城郡，分汝南立汝陰郡，合陳郡于梁國。
units.en: Once Sima Yan took the throne he added Xiangcheng from Yingchuan, Ruoyin from Runan, and folded Chen into Liang.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the mandate, again split Yingchuan to establish Xiangcheng commandery, split Runan to establish Ruoyin commandery, and combined Chen commandery into Liang kingdom.

units.en: Emperor Hui carved Xincai from Ruyin, Chen from Liang, and Nandun from Runan.
units.literal: Emperor Hui split off Xincai from Ruyin, established Chen Commandery from the Liang kingdom, and established Nandun from Runan.

units.zh: 永嘉之亂，豫州淪沒石氏。
units.en: Yongjia's chaos surrendered Yuzhou to the Shi regime.
units.literal: In the Yongjia turmoil, Yuzhou fell to the Shi clan.

units.zh: 元帝渡江，以春穀縣僑立襄城郡及繁昌縣。
units.en: After Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, exiles from Chungu founded paper Xiangcheng commandery and Fanchang county.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan crossed the river and, using Chungu County, sojourning established Xiangcheng Commandery and Fanchang County.

units.zh: 成帝乃僑立豫州於江淮之間，居蕪湖。
units.en: Emperor Cheng later staged Yuzhou between the Yangzi and Huai with its seat at Wuhu.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng then sojourning established Yuzhou between the Jiang and Huai, residing at Wuhu.

units.zh: 時淮南入北，乃分丹楊僑立淮南郡，居于湖。
units.en: When Huainan passed north, Danyang exiles papered Huainan commandery at Yuhu.
units.literal: At that time Huainan fell to the north; therefore Danyang was split to sojourning establish Huainan Commandery, residing at Yuhu.

units.zh: 又以舊當塗縣流人渡江，僑立爲縣，并淮南、廬江、安豐並屬豫州。
units.en: Dangtu refugees crossing south gained a paper county, and Huainan, Lujiang, and Anfeng were folded into Yuzhou.
units.literal: Further, using refugees from the old Dangtu County who crossed the river, a sojourning county was established; together Huainan, Lujiang, and Anfeng all belonged to Yuzhou.

units.en: In the first year of Ningkang, the garrison was moved to Gushu.
units.literal: In the first year of Ningkang, the garrison moved to Gushu.

units.zh: 孝武改蘄春縣爲蘄陽縣，因新蔡縣人於漢九江王黥布舊城置南新蔡郡，屬南豫州。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu renamed Qichun Qiyang and planted South Xincai on King Qing Bu's old Jiujiang seat for Xincai exiles under South Yuzhou.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu changed Qichun County to Qiyang County; because of people from Xincai County, at the old city of Han's King Qing Bu of Jiujiang he established South Xincai Commandery, belonging to South Yuzhou.

units.zh: 又於漢廬江郡之南部置晉熙郡。
units.en: He also drew Jinxi commandery from southern Han Lujiang.
units.literal: Further, on the southern part of Han's Lujiang Commandery he established Jinxi Commandery.

units.zh: 案禹貢、《周禮》並爲河內之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。
units.en: Both classics treat the belt inside the Yellow River as one of Shun's twelve pastorates.
units.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu and the Rites of Zhou, both are the land within the river; Shun established twelve herds—this is one of them.

units.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「昴畢散爲冀州，分爲趙國。」
units.en: The Yuanming Bao reads the Mao-Bi stars as seed of Jizhou and the Zhao heartland.'
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says: "The Mao and Bi constellations scatter and become Jizhou, splitting to form the state of Zhao."

units.zh: 其地有險有易，帝王所都，亂則冀安，弱則冀強，荒則冀豐。
units.en: Its terrain mixes passes and easy ground, so every dynasty built a capital there: when the realm totters Ji still feels safe, when armies weaken Ji stays strong, when fields fail Ji still feeds the north.
units.literal: Its land has defiles and plains; emperors and kings made capitals there; in disorder then Ji is secure, in weakness then Ji is strong, in famine then Ji is abundant.

units.zh: 舜以冀州南北闊大，分衛以西爲并州，燕以北爲幽州，周人因焉。
units.en: Shun sliced the overwide Ji plain into Bing west of Wei and You north of Yan, and Zhou kept his lines.
units.literal: Shun because Jizhou north-south was vast, split west of Wei as Bingzhou, north of Yan as Youzhou; Zhou people followed this.

units.zh: 及漢武置十三州，以其地依舊名爲冀州，歷後漢至晉不改。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Han reused the classical Jizhou label for the same ground, and Han and Jin never renamed it.
units.literal: When Han Wu established thirteen provinces, taking its land by the old name called Jizhou; through Later Han down to Jin not changed.

units.literal: In the second Taixing year he arrogated the imperial style at Xiangguo and styled his state Zhao.

units.en: Murong Jun later toppled Shi Le's Zhao, then Fu Jian swept away the Murongs as well.
units.literal: Later [Zhao] was extinguished by Murong Jun; the Murong house was in turn destroyed by Fu Jian.

units.zh: 孝武太元八年，堅敗，其地入慕容垂。
units.en: When Fu Jian shattered in Taiyuan 8, every acre slid to Murong Chui.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era, after Fu Jian's defeat the territory passed to Murong Chui.

units.zh: 垂僭號於中山，是爲後燕。
units.en: Murong Chui then enthroned himself at Zhongshan as Later Yan.
units.literal: Chui arrogated the title at Zhongshan; this is Later Yan.

units.en: Wei eventually snuffed out Later Yan.
units.literal: Later Yan was finally extinguished by Wei.

units.zh: 案《禹貢》冀州之域，舜置十二牧，則其一也。
units.en: The Jizhou belt mapped in the Tribute of Yu was one of the twelve pastorates Shun ordained.
units.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, the Jizhou domain—Shun established twelve herds; this is one of them.

units.en: The Rites of Zhou reads: "The northeast bears the name Youzhou."
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou: "The northeast is called Youzhou."

units.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「箕星散爲幽州，分爲燕國。」
units.en: The Yuanming Bao says, "The Ji stars scatter and become Youzhou, splitting to form the state of Yan."
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says: "The Ji stars scatter and become Youzhou, splitting to form the state of Yan."

units.zh: 言北方太陰，故以幽冥爲號。
units.en: Commentators tied the label to the northern yin pole, hence a name evoking shadowed northlands.
units.literal: It speaks of the northern yin; therefore the name uses darkness and shadow.

units.zh: 武王定殷，封召公於燕，其後與六國俱稱王。
units.en: After King Wu overthrew the Shang, Duke Shao received Yan; later Yan joined the six Warring States in taking royal titles.
units.literal: King Wu settled Yin and enfeoffed Duke Shao in Yan; afterward Yan and the six states alike styled themselves kings.

units.zh: 及秦滅燕，以爲漁陽、上谷、右北平、遼西、遼東五郡。
units.en: Qin's conquest carved Yan into Yuyang, Shanggu, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong commanderies.
units.literal: When Qin extinguished Yan, it made Yuyang, Shanggu, Right Beiping, Liaoxi, and Liaodong—five commanderies.

units.en: Han Gaozu peeled Zhuo Commandery out of Shanggu.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han split off Zhuo Commandery from Shanggu.

units.zh: 武帝置十三州，幽州依舊名不改。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Han fixed thirteen inspectorates and left the classical Youzhou label in place.
units.literal: Emperor Wu established thirteen provinces; Youzhou kept the old name unchanged.

units.zh: 其後開東邊，置玄菟、樂浪等郡，亦皆屬焉。
units.en: Later Han pushed east and layered Xuantu, Lelang, and other frontier commands under Youzhou.
units.literal: Afterward the eastern marches were opened and Xuantu, Lelang, and other commanderies were established; all likewise belonged to it.

units.zh: 元鳳元年，改燕曰廣陽郡。
units.en: Yuanfeng year one rechristened the old Yan seat as Guangyang Commandery.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, Yan was changed to Guangyang Commandery.

units.zh: 幽州所部凡九郡，至晉不改。
units.en: Youzhou wrapped nine commanderies, and Jin kept that roster.

units.en: After Chui died, Murong Bao withdrew toward Helong.
units.literal: When Chui died, Bao relocated to Helong.

units.zh: 案禹貢冀州之域，於周爲幽州界，漢屬右北平郡。
units.en: The classical tribute lists count it as Ji soil; Zhou drew Youzhou's border here; Han folded it into Youbeiping.
units.literal: By the reckoning of the "Tribute of Yu," this lay within Ji Province; under Zhou it marked the Youzhou frontier; Han attached it to Youbeiping Commandery.

units.zh: 後漢末，公孫度自號平州牧。
units.en: Near Later Han's end Gongsun Du claimed the Pingzhou governorship.
units.literal: Late in Later Han, Gongsun Du styled himself governor of Pingzhou.

units.zh: 及其子康、康子文懿並擅據遼東，東夷九種皆服事焉。
units.en: He and his son Kang, then Kang's heir Wenyi, held Liaodong until every Eastern Yi tribe owed them allegiance.
units.literal: Together with his son Kang and Kang's son Wenyi he seized Liaodong; all nine eastern Yi peoples submitted.

units.zh: 魏置東夷校尉，居襄平，而分遼東、昌黎、玄菟、帶方、樂浪五郡爲平州，後還合爲幽州。
units.en: Wei placed a Colonel for the Eastern Yi at Xiangping, separated Liaodong, Changli, Xuantu, Daifang, and Lelang into the five commanderies of Pingzhou, and later merged them back into Youzhou.
units.literal: Wei established the Colonel of Eastern Yi, seated at Xiangping, and split Liaodong, Changli, Xuantu, Daifang, and Lelang—five commanderies—into Pingzhou; later they were merged back into Youzhou.

units.zh: 及文懿滅後，有護東夷校尉，居襄平。
units.en: After Wenyi was extinguished, there was a Protector-Colonel of the Eastern Yi at Xiangping.
units.literal: After Wenyi was extinguished, there was a protector-colonel of Eastern Yi, dwelling at Xiangping.

units.zh: 咸寧二年十月，分昌黎、遼東、玄菟、帶方、樂浪等郡國五置平州。
units.en: In Xianning 2, tenth month, the court commissioned Pingzhou from Changli, Liaodong, Xuantu, Daifang, and Lelang.
units.literal: In the tenth month of Xianning 2, Changli, Liaodong, Xuantu, Daifang, Lelang and other commands—five units—were set up as Pingzhou.

units.zh: 統縣二十六，戶一萬八千一百。
units.en: Twenty-six counties totaling eighteen thousand one hundred households.
units.literal: It governs twenty-six counties; households eighteen thousand one hundred.

units.literal: Annotation marker [26].

units.literal: Changli Commandery.

units.literal: 〈Under Han it belonged to the dependent-state colonel of Liaodong; Wei established it as a commandery.

units.literal: It governs two counties; households nine hundred.〉

units.literal: Liaodong kingdom.

units.zh: 漢光武以遼東等屬青州後，還幽州。
units.en: Emperor Guangwu briefly parked Liaodong under Qingzhou before folding it back into Youzhou.
units.literal: Han Guangwu attached Liaodong and others to Qingzhou, then later restored them to Youzhou.

units.en: Eight counties and five thousand four hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs eight counties; households five thousand four hundred.〉

units.en: Xiangping county.
units.literal: Xiangping.

units.literal: 〈Seat of the Eastern Yi colonel.〉

units.en: Wen, Jujiu, Lejiu, Anshi, Xi'anping, Xinchang, and Licheng counties.
units.literal: Wen Jujiu Lejiu Anshi Xi'anping Xinchang Licheng.

units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.literal: It governs six counties; households three thousand seven hundred.〉

units.literal: 〈The land Zhou enfeoffed to Jizi.〉

units.en: Tunyou, Hunmi, and Suicheng counties.
units.literal: Tunyou Hunmi Suicheng.

units.en: 〈The Long Wall line starts from this ridge.〉
units.literal: 〈Where Qin began building the Long Wall.〉

units.en: Lufang and Siwang counties.
units.literal: Lufang Siwang.

units.literal: Xuantu Commandery.

units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.literal: It governs three counties; households three thousand two hundred.〉

units.en: Gaogouli, Wangping, and Gaoxian counties.
units.literal: Gaogouli Wangping Gaoxian.

units.literal: Daifang Commandery.

units.literal: 〈Gongsun Du established it.

units.literal: It governs seven counties; households four thousand nine hundred.〉

units.zh: 帶方 列口 南新 長岑 提奚 含資 海冥
units.en: Daifang, Liekou, Nanxin, Changcen, Tixi, Hanzai, and Haiming counties.
units.literal: Daifang Liekou Nanxin Changcen Tixi Hanzai Haiming.

units.zh: 平州初置，以慕容廆爲刺史，遂屬永嘉之亂，廆爲眾所推。
units.en: When Pingzhou was first established, Murong Hui was made its inspector; then, amid the Yongjia turmoil, Hui was acclaimed by the multitude.
units.literal: When Pingzhou was first established, Murong Hui was appointed inspector; then came the Yongjia turmoil and Hui was acclaimed by the multitude.

units.en: His grandson Murong Jun later carried the court to Ji.
units.literal: His grandson Jun moved the capital to Ji.

units.zh: 其後慕容垂子寶又遷于和龍，自幽州至於廬溥鎮以南地入於魏。
units.en: Afterward Murong Chui's son Bao again moved to Helong; from Youzhou down to the land south of Lupu garrison fell into Wei hands.
units.literal: Afterward Murong Chui's son Bao again moved to Helong; from Youzhou down to the territory south of Lupu garrison fell into Wei hands.

units.zh: 慕容熙以幽州刺史鎮令支，青州刺史鎮新城，并州刺史鎮凡城，營州刺史鎮宿軍，冀州刺史鎮肥如。
units.en: Murong Xi posted the Youzhou inspector at Lingzhi, the Qingzhou inspector at Xincheng, the Bingzhou inspector at Fancheng, the Yingzhou inspector at Sujun, and the Jizhou inspector at Feiru.
units.literal: Murong Xi posted the Youzhou inspector at Lingzhi, the Qingzhou inspector at Xincheng, the Bingzhou inspector at Fancheng, the Yingzhou inspector at Sujun, and the Jizhou inspector at Feiru.

units.zh: 高雲以幽、冀二州牧鎮肥如，并州刺史鎮白狼。
units.en: Gao Yun paired You-Ji shepherds at Feiru while anchoring Bingzhou at Bailang.
units.literal: Gao Yun used the joint shepherd of You and Ji at Feiru and stationed the Bingzhou inspector at Bailang.

units.zh: 後爲馮跋所篡，跋僭號於和龍，是爲後燕，卒滅於魏。
units.en: Later Feng Ba usurped him; Ba arrogated an imperial style at Helong, still reckoned as Later Yan, and finally fell to Wei.
units.literal: Later Feng Ba usurped him; Ba arrogated an imperial style at Helong—still reckoned as Later Yan—and finally fell to Wei.

units.zh: 案《禹貢》蓋冀州之域，舜置十二牧，則其一也。
units.en: Classical geography treats this ground as Jizhou country, one of Shun's twelve pastorates.
units.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, broadly the Jizhou domain—Shun established twelve herds; this is one of them.

units.en: The Rites of Zhou names due north Bingzhou and anchors it on Mount Heng.
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou: due north is called Bingzhou; its guardian mountain is Mount Heng.

units.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「營室流爲并州，分爲衛國。」
units.en: The Yuanming Bao says, "Yingshi flows aside to become Bingzhou, splitting to form the state of Wei."
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuanming Bao says: "Yingshi flows aside to become Bingzhou, splitting to form the state of Wei."

units.zh: 州不以衛水爲號，又不以山爲稱，而云并者，蓋以其在兩谷之間也。
units.en: The name did not follow the Wei River or a peak; commentators said bing marked the belt between twin valleys.
units.literal: The province is not named for the Wei River, nor called for a mountain; yet it is called Bing—probably because it lies between two valleys.

units.zh: 漢武帝置十三州，并州依舊名不改，統上黨、太原、雲中、上郡、雁門、代郡、定襄、五原、西河、朔方十郡，又別置朔方刺史。
units.en: Han Wudi kept the classical Bingzhou label over ten northern commands and added a separate Shuofang inspector.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Han established thirteen provinces; Bingzhou kept the old name unchanged, governing Shangdang, Taiyuan, Yunzhong, Shang, Yanmen, Dai, Dingxiang, Wuyuan, Xihe, and Shuofang—ten commanderies—and separately set a Shuofang inspector.

units.zh: 後漢建武十一年，省朔方入并州。
units.en: Later Han Jianwu eleven merged Shuofang back into Bingzhou.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Jianwu under Later Han, Shuofang was abolished and folded into Bingzhou.

units.zh: 靈帝末，羌胡大擾，定襄、雲中、五原、朔方、上郡等五郡並流徙分散。
units.en: Lingdi's last years saw Qiang and Hu turmoil scatter Dingxiang, Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, and Shang.
units.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling, Qiang and Hu raiders greatly disturbed the land; Dingxiang, Yunzhong, Wuyuan, Shuofang, and Shang—five commanderies—were all displaced and scattered.

units.en: Jian'an eighteen folded the command into Jizhou.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jian'an it was abolished and folded into Jizhou.

units.zh: 二十年，始集塞下荒地立新興郡，後又分上黨立樂平郡。
units.en: Jian'an twenty planted Xinxing on frontier waste, then carved Leping out of Shangdang.
units.literal: In the twentieth year they first gathered waste land below the passes and established Xinxing Commandery; later they split off Leping Commandery from Shangdang.

units.zh: 魏黃初元年，復置并州，自陘嶺以北並棄之，至晉因而不改。
units.en: Wei Huangchu one revived Bingzhou but abandoned everything north of Xing Ridge, a line Jin kept.
units.literal: In the first year of Huangchu under Wei, Bingzhou was restored; north of Xing Ridge all was abandoned, and Jin followed without change.

units.zh: 并州統郡國六，縣四十五，戶五萬九千三百。
units.en: Western Jin Bingzhou counted six jurisdictions, forty-five counties, and fifty-nine thousand three hundred households.
units.literal: Bingzhou governed six commanderies and kingdoms, forty-five counties, households fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

units.literal: Taiyuan kingdom: Qin established it.

units.literal: It governs thirteen counties; households fourteen thousand.〉

units.literal: 〈Marquis chancellor.〉

units.en: Yangqu, Yuci, Yuli, Yu, Langmeng, Yangyi, Daling, Qi, Pingtao, Jingling, Zhongdu, and Wu counties.
units.literal: Yangqu Yuci Yuli Yu Langmeng Yangyi Daling Qi Pingtao Jingling Zhongdu Wu.

units.literal: Shangdang Commandery.

units.literal: 〈Qin established it.

units.literal: It governs ten counties; households thirteen thousand.〉

units.literal: Lu Tunliu Huguan Changzi Xuan Shi Gaodu Tongdi Nie Xiangyuan Wuxiang.

units.literal: Xihe kingdom.

units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.literal: It governs four counties; households six thousand three hundred.〉

units.en: Lishi, Xicheng, Zhongyang, and Jiexiu counties.
units.literal: Lishi Xicheng Zhongyang Jiexiu.

units.literal: Leping Commandery.

units.literal: 〈Established in the Taishi era.

units.literal: It governs five counties; households four thousand three hundred.〉

units.literal: Zhan Shang'ai Shouyang Liaoyang Leping.

units.literal: Yanmen Commandery.

units.literal: 〈Qin established it.

units.zh: 統縣八，戶一萬二千七百。〉
units.en: Eight counties and twelve thousand seven hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs eight counties; households twelve thousand seven hundred.〉

units.zh: 廣武 崞 𣳫陶 平城 葰人 繁畤 原平 馬邑
units.en: Guangwu, Guo, Yituo, Pingcheng, Junren, Fanzi, Yuanping, and Mayi counties.
units.literal: Guangwu Guo Yituo Pingcheng Junren Fanzi Yuanping Mayi.

units.en: The Xinxing commandery.
units.literal: Xinxing Commandery.

units.en: 〈Wei carved it out.
units.literal: 〈Wei established it.

units.en: Five counties and nine thousand households.〉
units.literal: It governs five counties; households nine thousand.〉

units.zh: 九原定襄雲中廣牧晉昌惠帝改新興爲晉昌郡。
units.en: Jiuyuan, Dingxiang, Yunzhong, Guangmu, and Jinchang counties sat under Jinchang commandery after Hui renamed Xinxing.
units.literal: Jiuyuan, Dingxiang, Yunzhong, Guangmu, Jinchang—Emperor Hui changed Xinxing to Jinchang Commandery.

units.zh: 及永興元年，劉元海僭號於平陽，稱漢，於是并州之地皆爲元海所有。
units.en: Yongxing one saw Liu Yuanhai crown himself Han at Pingyang and seize Bingzhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongxing, Liu Yuanhai arrogated the title at Pingyang, styled himself Han; then the land of Bingzhou all fell to Yuanhai.

units.zh: 元海乃以雍州刺史鎮平陽，幽州刺史鎮離石。
units.en: Yuanhai stationed the Yongzhou inspector at Pingyang and the Youzhou inspector at Lishi.
units.literal: Yuanhai then posted the Yongzhou inspector at Pingyang and the Youzhou inspector at Lishi.

units.zh: 及劉聰攻陷洛陽，置左右司隸，各領戶二十餘萬，萬戶置一內史，凡內史四十三人，單于左右輔各主六夷。
units.en: Liu Cong's Luoyang conquest brought paired metropolitan superintendents over two hundred thousand households each, forty-three inner governors, and Chanyu assistants over the Six Yi.
units.literal: When Liu Cong captured Luoyang, he established left and right metropolitan superintendents, each administering more than two hundred thousand households; for every ten thousand households one inner governor was set—forty-three inner governors in all—and the left and right assistants to the Chanyu each oversaw the Six Yi.

units.zh: 又置殷、衛、東梁、西河陽、北兗五州，以懷安新附。
units.en: Five new provinces—Yin, Wei, East Liang, West Heyang, and North Yan—were meant to settle fresh submissions.
units.literal: He further established Yin, Wei, East Liang, West Heyang, and North Yan—five provinces—to soothe newly submitted peoples.

units.zh: 劉曜徙都長安，其平陽以東地入石勒。
units.en: When Liu Yao shifted court to Chang'an, everything east of Pingyang fell to Shi Le.
units.literal: Liu Yao moved the capital to Chang'an; east of Pingyang the land passed to Shi Le.

units.en: Shi Le pacified Shuofang and again established Shuozhou.
units.literal: Le pacified Shuofang and again established Shuozhou.

units.zh: 自惠懷之間，離石縣荒廢，勒於其處置永石郡，又別置武鄉郡。
units.en: Between Hui and Huai, abandoned Lishi became Yongshi commandery under Le, with Wuxiang split off beside it.
units.literal: From the time between Emperors Hui and Huai, Lishi County lay waste; Le there established Yongshi Commandery and separately set Wuxiang Commandery.

units.zh: 及苻堅、姚興、赫連勃勃，并州並徙置河東，又姚興以河東爲并、冀二州云。
units.en: Fu Jian, Yao Xing, and Helian Bobo kept shifting Bingzhou into Hedong; Yao Xing even paired Bing and Ji there.
units.literal: Under Fu Jian, Yao Xing, and Helian Bobo, Bingzhou was altogether shifted and planted in Hedong; moreover Yao Xing made Hedong serve as both Bing and Ji provinces.

units.zh: 案《禹貢》黑水、西河之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。
units.en: The Black River and Western River belt in the Tribute of Yu was another of Shun's twelve pastorates.
units.literal: Examining the Tribute of Yu, the land of the Black River and Western River—Shun established twelve pastors; this is one of them.

units.zh: 以其四山之地，故以雍名焉。
units.en: Four enclosing mountains gave the province the name Yong.
units.literal: Because of its four-mountain land, it was therefore named Yong.

units.zh: 亦謂西北之位，陽所不及，陰氣雍閼也。
units.en: Northwest geography lay beyond the sun's reach, where yin qi pooled and stagnated.
units.literal: It is also said that in the northwest position yang does not reach, and yin qi is blocked and stagnant.

units.en: The Rites of Zhou names the west Yongzhou.
units.literal: The Rites of Zhou: west is called Yongzhou.

units.en: It also swallowed the Liangzhou ground Yu had mapped.
units.literal: Broadly it combined Yu's Liangzhou territory.

units.zh: 周自武王克殷，都於酆鎬，雍州爲王畿。
units.en: After King Wu of Zhou overthrew Yin, Feng and Hao made Yongzhou the royal heartland.
units.literal: From Zhou, when King Wu conquered Yin, the capital was at Feng and Hao; Yongzhou was the royal domain.

units.zh: 及平王東遷洛邑，以岐酆之地賜秦襄公，則爲秦地，累世都之，至始皇遂平六國。
units.en: King Ping's eastern move handed the western Zhou domain to Duke Xiang of Qin, and Qin kept that capital line until the First Emperor unified the realm.
units.literal: When King Ping moved east to Luoyi, he granted the Qi-Feng lands to Duke Xiang of Qin; then it became Qin territory, generation after generation made capital there, until the First Emperor finally pacified the six states.

units.en: Han succeeded Qin and again centered the throne there.
units.literal: Qin fell, and Han again made it capital.

units.zh: 及武帝置十三州，其地以西偏爲涼州，其餘並屬司隸，不統於州。
units.en: Han Wudi carved Liangzhou from the western fringe and left the rest under the metropolitan belt outside provincial rule.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu established thirteen provinces, its western fringe became Liangzhou; the rest all belonged to the metropolitan superintendent and were not governed as a province.

units.zh: 後漢光武都洛陽，關中復置雍州。
units.en: Guangwu's Luoyang court briefly restored Yongzhou in Guanzhong.
units.literal: Later Han Emperor Guangwu made Luoyang capital; Guanzhong again had Yongzhou established.

units.zh: 後罷，復置司隸校尉，統三輔如舊。
units.en: The province was dropped again and the metropolitan superintendent reclaimed the Three Adjuncts.
units.literal: Later it was abolished; the metropolitan superintendent was restored, governing the Three Adjuncts as before.

units.zh: 獻帝時又置雍州，自三輔距西域皆屬焉。
units.en: Emperor Xian revived Yongzhou from the Three Adjuncts west toward the Western Regions.
units.literal: In Emperor Xian's time Yongzhou was again established; from the Three Adjuncts to the Western Regions all belonged to it.

units.zh: 魏文帝即位，分河西爲涼州，分隴右爲秦州，改京兆尹爲太守，馮翊、扶風各除左右，仍以三輔屬司隸。
units.en: Wei Wendi split Liangzhou from Hexi and Qinzhou from Longyou, demoted Jingzhao to a prefecture, and kept the Three Adjuncts under metropolitan rule.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei took the throne, he split Hexi as Liangzhou and Longyou as Qinzhou, changed the Jingzhao intendant to a grand administrator, removed the left and right designations from Fengyi and Fufeng, and still left the Three Adjuncts under the metropolitan superintendent.

units.zh: 晉初於長安置雍州，統郡國七，縣三十九，戶九萬九千五百。
units.en: Early Jin staged Yongzhou at Chang'an with seven jurisdictions, thirty-nine counties, and ninety-nine thousand five hundred households.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin, Yongzhou was placed at Chang'an, governing seven commanderies and kingdoms, thirty-nine counties, households ninety-nine thousand five hundred.

units.literal: Jingzhao Commandery: Han established it.

units.en: Nine counties and forty thousand households.〉
units.literal: It governs nine counties; households forty thousand.〉

units.en: Chang'an, Duling, Bacheng, Lantian, Gaolu, and Wannian counties.
units.literal: Chang'an Duling Bacheng Lantian Gaolu Wannian.

units.literal: 〈Formerly Liyang county.〉

units.literal: 〈The town of Duke Huan of Zheng, younger brother of King Xuan of Zhou.〉

units.literal: 〈Han established it; called Left Fengyi.

units.literal: It governs eight counties; households seven thousand seven hundred.〉

units.literal: 〈Formerly Dali; Qin captured it and renamed it.

units.zh: 有河水祠，祠臨晉水，故名。〉
units.en: It drew the name from the Linjin River altar beside the Yellow River.〉
units.literal: There is a River God shrine; the shrine faces Linjin water—hence the name.〉

units.en: Xiagui county.
units.literal: Xiagui.

units.zh: 〈秦武公伐邽戎，置有上邽，故加「下」。〉
units.en: 〈When Duke Wu of Qin smashed the Gui Rong he carved out this county; Shanggui already lay upstream, so the name was prefixed with "Lower."〉
units.literal: 〈Duke Wu of Qin attacked the Gui Rong and set up the county; because there was already Shanggui, he prefixed 「lower」 to the name.〉

units.en: Chongquan and Pinyang counties.
units.literal: Chongquan Pinyang.

units.zh: 惠帝即位，改扶風國爲秦國。
units.en: Emperor Hui elevated Fufeng into the Qin princedom.
units.literal: When Emperor Hui took the throne he renamed the Fufeng kingdom the Qin kingdom.

units.en: The court shifted its capital.
units.literal: He moved the capital.

units.zh: 建興之後，雍州沒於劉聰。
units.en: After the Jianxing era, Yongzhou was lost to Liu Cong.
units.literal: After Jianxing, Yong Province fell to Liu Cong.

units.zh: 及劉曜徙都長安，改號曰趙，以秦、涼二州牧鎮上邽，朔州牧鎮高平，幽州刺史鎮北地，并州牧鎮蒲阪。
units.en: Liu Yao crowned himself at Chang'an as Zhao and scattered inspectors—Qin-Liang at Shanggui, Shuozhou at Gaoping, Youzhou on Beidi soil, Bingzhou guarding Puban.
units.literal: When Liu Yao moved the capital to Chang'an he changed his dynastic title to Zhao; he stationed the joint shepherds of Qin and Liang at Shanggui, the Shuozhou shepherd at Gaoping, the Youzhou inspector at Beidi, and the Bingzhou shepherd at Puban.

units.en: Shi Le seized Chang'an and resurrected Yongzhou.
units.literal: Shi Le captured Chang'an and restored Yongzhou.

units.zh: 石氏既敗，苻健僭據關中，又都長安，是爲前秦。
units.en: Once the Shi house fell, Fu Jian (the Former Qin founder) clamped Guanzhong and enthroned Former Qin at Chang'an.
units.literal: After the Shi clan collapsed, Fu Jian seized Guanzhong and again made Chang'an his capital—this is Former Qin.

units.zh: 於是乃於雍州置司隸校尉，以豫州刺史鎮許昌，秦州刺史鎮上邽，荊州刺史鎮豐陽，洛州刺史鎮宜陽，并州刺史鎮蒲阪。
units.en: They carved out a metropolitan colonelcy at Yongzhou while pinning Yuzhou at Xuchang, Qinzhou at Shanggui, Jingzhou at Fengyang, Luozhou at Yiyang, and Bingzhou at Puban.
units.literal: Thereupon they placed a metropolitan colonel at Yongzhou, stationed the Yuzhou inspector at Xuchang, the Qinzhou inspector at Shanggui, the Jingzhou inspector at Fengyang, the Luozhou inspector at Yiyang, and the Bingzhou inspector at Puban.

units.zh: 苻堅時，分司隸爲雍州，分京兆爲咸陽郡，洛州刺史鎮陝城。
units.en: Fu Jian split metropolitan territory into Yongzhou, peeled Xianyang from Jingzhao, and slid Luozhou forward to Shancheng.
units.literal: Under Fu Jian the metropolitan seat became Yongzhou, Jingzhao was split into Xianyang Commandery, and the Luozhou inspector moved to Shancheng.

units.zh: 滅燕之後，分幽州置平州，鎮龍城，幽州刺史鎮薊城，河州刺史鎮枹罕，并州刺史鎮晉陽，豫州刺史鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，雍州刺史鎮蒲阪。
units.en: After Yan was destroyed, Pingzhou was separated from Youzhou and stationed at Longcheng; the inspector of Youzhou was stationed at Jicheng, the inspector of Hezhou at Fuhan, the inspector of Bingzhou at Jinyang, the inspector of Yuzhou at Luoyang, the inspector of Yanzhou at Cangyuan, and the inspector of Yongzhou at Puban.
units.literal: After Yan was extinguished they carved Pingzhou from Youzhou with its seat at Longcheng; they stationed the Youzhou inspector at Ji, the Hezhou inspector at Fuhan, the Bingzhou inspector at Jinyang, the Yuzhou inspector at Luoyang, the Yanzhou inspector at Cangyuan, and the Yongzhou inspector at Puban.

units.zh: 於是移洛州居豐陽，以許昌置東豫州，以荊州刺史鎮襄陽，徐州刺史鎮彭城。
units.en: Luozhou slid south to Fengyang, eastern Yuzhou anchored Xuchang, while Jingzhou and Xuzhou watched Xiangyang and Pengcheng.
units.literal: Then Luozhou was shifted to Fengyang, Dong-Yuzhou was established at Xuchang, the Jingzhou inspector moved to Xiangyang, and the Xuzhou inspector to Pengcheng.

units.zh: 既而姚萇滅苻氏，是爲後秦。
units.en: Yao Chang soon erased Former Qin and styled Later Qin.
units.literal: Soon Yao Chang extinguished the Fu clan—this is Later Qin.

units.zh: 及萇子興克洛陽，以并、冀二州牧鎮蒲阪，豫州牧鎮洛陽，兗州刺史鎮倉垣，分司隸領北五郡，置雍州刺史鎮安定。
units.en: Yao Xing seized Luoyang, stacked Bing-Ji shepherds at Puban, Yu power at Luoyang, Yanzhou at Cangyuan, carved northern metropolitan belts, and parked Yongzhou at Anding.
units.literal: When Chang's son Xing took Luoyang he stationed joint Bing-Ji shepherds at Puban, the Yu shepherd at Luoyang, the Yanzhou inspector at Cangyuan, split the metropolitan northern five commanderies, and placed a Yongzhou inspector at Anding.

units.zh: 及姚泓爲劉裕所滅，其地尋入赫連勃勃。
units.en: Yao Hong perished before Liu Yu and Helian Bobo swallowed the plateau.
units.literal: When Yao Hong fell to Liu Yu the territory soon passed to Helian Bobo.

units.zh: 勃勃僭號於統萬，是爲夏。
units.en: Helian Bobo crowned himself at Tongwan as the Xia dynasty.
units.literal: Bobo arrogated his title at Tongwan—this is Xia.

units.zh: 置幽州牧於大城，又平劉義真於長安，遣子璝鎮焉，號曰南臺。
units.en: He named a Youzhou shepherd at Dacheng, crushed Liu Yizhen at Chang'an, left son Gui as viceroy, and dubbed the court Southern Terrace.
units.literal: He placed a Youzhou shepherd at Dacheng; after defeating Liu Yizhen at Chang'an he sent his son Gui to hold it, styled the Southern Terrace.

units.zh: 以朔州牧鎮三城，秦州刺史鎮杏城，雍州刺史鎮陰密，并州刺史鎮蒲阪，梁州牧鎮安定，北秦州刺史鎮武功，豫州牧鎮李閏，[30]荊州刺史鎮陝，其州郡之名並不可知也。
units.en: The governor of Shuozhou was stationed at Sancheng, the inspector of Qinzhou at Xingcheng, the inspector of Yongzhou at Yinmi, the inspector of Bingzhou at Puban, the governor of Liangzhou at Anding, the inspector of Northern Qinzhou at Wugong, the governor of Yuzhou at Lijian,[30] and the inspector of Jingzhou at Shan; the exact prefectural and commandery names can no longer be known.
units.literal: He stationed the Shuozhou shepherd at Sancheng, the Qinzhou inspector at Xingcheng, the Yongzhou inspector at Yinmi, the Bingzhou inspector at Puban, the Liangzhou shepherd at Anding, the Northern Qinzhou inspector at Wugong, the Yu shepherd at Lijian,[30] and the Jingzhou inspector at Shan—the roster of prefectures can no longer be reconciled.

units.zh: 然自元帝渡江，所置州亦皆遙領。
units.en: After Emperor Yuan crossed the Great River, northern provinces became empty titles on the left bank.
units.literal: Yet from the time Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangtze every northern province established on the south shore existed only as nominal postings.

units.zh: 初以魏該爲雍州刺史，鎮酇城，尋省，僑立始平郡，寄居武當城。
units.en: Wei Gai briefly held Yongzhou at Zancheng until the office vanished and Shiping sojourned at Wudang.
units.literal: First Wei Gai served as Yongzhou inspector at Zancheng; that post was soon abolished and a provisional Shiping Commandery lodged at Wudang fortress.

units.zh: 有秦國流人至江南，改堂邑爲秦郡，僑立尉氏縣屬焉。
units.en: Qin exiles triggered renaming Tangyi to Qin Commandery with Weishi nested inside.
units.literal: When refugees from the Qin princedom reached the southlands Tangyi was renamed Qin Commandery and they planted Weishi County beneath it.

units.zh: 康帝時，庾翼爲荊州刺史，遷鎮襄陽。
units.en: In Emperor Kang's time, Yu Yi served as inspector of Jingzhou and moved his seat to Xiangyang.
units.literal: Under Emperor Kang Yu Yi became Jingzhou inspector and shifted his seat to Xiangyang.

units.zh: 其後秦雍流人多南出樊沔，孝武始於襄陽僑立雍州，仍立京兆、始平、扶風、河南、廣平、義成、北河南七郡，並屬襄陽。
units.en: After Qin-Yong exiles poured south through Fan and Mian, Emperor Xiaowu first established a provisional Yongzhou at Xiangyang together with seven attached commanderies.
units.literal: Later refugees from Qin and Yong poured out through Fan and Mian; Emperor Xiaowu first planted a provisional Yongzhou at Xiangyang together with seven commanderies—Jingzhao, Shiping, Fufeng, Henan, Guangping, Yicheng, and Northern Henan—all subordinate to Xiangyang.

units.en: Xiangyang itself once answered only to Jingzhou.
units.literal: Xiangyang had formerly belonged to Jingzhou.

units.zh: 案禹貢雍州之西界，周衰，其地爲狄。
units.en: By the Tribute of Yu this marked Yongzhou's western bound; when Zhou declined the land fell to the Di.
units.literal: By the reckoning of the "Tribute of Yu," this marked Yongzhou's western rim; when Zhou declined the land fell to the Di peoples.

units.zh: 秦興美陽甘泉宮，本匈奴鑄金人祭天之處。
units.en: Qin built the Ganquan palace at Meiyang, originally the place where the Xiongnu cast golden figures to sacrifice to Heaven.
units.literal: Qin raised its Ganquan palace at Meiyang—the place where the Xiongnu once cast golden men for Heaven sacrifice.

units.zh: 匈奴既失甘泉，又使休屠、渾邪王等居涼州之地。
units.en: Deprived of Ganquan, the Xiongnu parked Xiutu and Hunye across Liangzhou.
units.literal: After the Xiongnu lost Ganquan they stationed the Xiutu and Hunye kings across Liangzhou.

units.zh: 二王後以地降漢，漢置張掖、酒泉、敦煌、武威郡。
units.en: Their surrender let Han layer Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei.
units.literal: When both kings later surrendered their lands Han organized Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Wuwei commanderies.

units.zh: 其後又置金城郡，謂之河西五郡。
units.en: Jincheng joined to complete the five Hexi commands.
units.literal: Later Han added Jincheng—the so-called five Hexi commanderies.

units.zh: 漢改周之雍州爲涼州，蓋以地處西方，常寒涼也。
units.en: Han renamed Zhou's Yongzhou Liangzhou for its biting chill.
units.literal: Han redesignated Zhou's Yongzhou as Liangzhou because the climate stayed perennially cold.

units.zh: 地勢西北邪出，在南山之間，南隔西羌，西通西域，于時號爲斷匈奴右臂。
units.en: The corridor squeezes northwest between ranges, brushes western Qiang, and reaches the Tarim—Han strategists called it amputating the Xiongnu right arm.
units.literal: The terrain angles northwest between southern ranges; it borders the western Qiang on the south and opens toward the Western Regions—contemporaries called it severing the Xiongnu right arm.

units.zh: 獻帝時，涼州數有亂，河西五郡去州隔遠，於是乃別以爲雍州。
units.en: Emperor Xian's Liangzhou revolts forced the distant Hexi quintet to become their own Yongzhou.
units.literal: Under Emperor Xian Liangzhou suffered repeated revolts; the five Hexi commanderies lay too far from the provincial seat, so they were separately constituted as Yongzhou.

units.zh: 末又依古典定九州，乃合關右以爲雍州。
units.en: Late Han ritualists recombined the western march into one Yongzhou.
units.literal: Near the dynasty's end the classical nine provinces were invoked and everything west of the passes was folded back into Yongzhou.

units.zh: 魏時復分以爲涼州，刺史領戊己校尉，護西域，如漢故事，至晉不改。
units.en: Wei split Liangzhou anew, kept the Wuji colonel over the Silk Road, and Jin kept the mold.
units.literal: Under Wei it was split again into Liangzhou; the inspector retained the Wuji colonel and protected the Western Regions after Han precedent—Jin left that arrangement intact.

units.en: Eight commanderies, forty-six counties, thirty thousand seven hundred households.
units.literal: It governs eight commanderies, forty-six counties, and thirty thousand seven hundred households.

units.en: Guzang, Xuanwei, Yici, Cangsong, Xianmei, Lijian, and Fanhe counties.

units.en: Changpu, Dunhuang, Longle, Yangguan, Xiaogu, Guangzhi, Yihe, Ming'an,[32] Shenquan,[33] Yiwu, Xinxiang, and Ganqi counties.
units.literal: Changpu Dunhuang Longle Yangguan Xiaogu Guangzhi Yihe Ming'an[32] Shenquan[33] Yiwu Xinxiang Ganqi.

units.en: 〈Split from Zhangye when Wuwei prefect Zhang Ya memorialized Emperor Xiandi in Xingping 2.
units.literal: 〈Formerly subordinate to Zhangye; in Han Xiandi's Xingping 2 the Wuwei prefect Zhang Ya petitioned to establish it.

units.en: One county and two thousand five hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs one county; households two thousand five hundred.〉

units.literal: 〈The marsh lies southeast—the "drifting sands" of the Documents.〉

units.zh: 元康五年，惠帝分敦煌郡之宜禾、伊吾、冥安、深泉、廣至等五縣，分酒泉之沙頭縣，又別立會稽、新鄉，凡八縣爲晉昌郡。
units.en: Yuankang 5 carved Jinchang from Dunhuang and Jiuquan scraps plus two new seats.
units.literal: In Yuankang 5 Emperor Hui split Yihu, Yiwu, Ming'an, Shenquan, and Guangzhi—five counties from Dunhuang—and Sha tou county from Jiuquan, added Kuaiji and Xinxiang counties, and formed Jinchang Commandery from eight counties.

units.zh: 永寧中，張軌爲涼州刺史，鎮武威，上表請合秦雍流移人於姑臧西北，置武興郡，統武興、大城、烏支、襄武、晏然、新鄣、平狄、司監等縣。
units.en: Zhang Gui petitioned Yongning courts to plant Qin-Yong exiles northwest of Guzang inside Wu Xing Commandery.
units.literal: During Yongning Zhang Gui served as Liangzhou inspector at Wuwei and memorialized to settle refugees from Qin and Yong northwest of Guzang in Wu Xing Commandery with counties Wuxing, Dacheng, Wuzhi, Xiangwu, Yanran, Xinzhang, Pingdi, and Sijian.

units.zh: 又分西平界置晉興郡，統晉興、枹罕、永固、臨津、臨鄣、廣昌、大夏、遂興、罕唐、左南等縣。
units.en: From Xiping he sliced Jinxing Commandery—Jinxing, Fuhan, Yonggu, Linjin, and allies.
units.literal: He also split Xiping's border to create Jinxing Commandery, governing Jinxing, Fuhan, Yonggu, Linjin, Linzhang, Guangchang, Daxia, Suixing, Hantang, Zuonan, and other counties.

units.zh: 是時中原淪沒，元帝徙居江左，軌乃控據河西，稱晉正朔，是爲前涼。
units.en: As refugees fled the Yellow River plain, Zhang Gui kept Jin rites alive beyond the passes as Former Liang.
units.literal: While the Central Plains collapsed Emperor Yuan moved south; Zhang Gui held the Hexi corridor and observed Jin calendar—this is Former Liang.

units.zh: 及張寔，分金城之令居、枝陽二縣，又立永登縣，合三縣立廣武郡。
units.en: Zhang Shi peeled Lingju and Zhiyang off Jincheng, added Yongdeng, and welded the trio into Guangwu Commandery.
units.literal: Afterward Zhang Shi split Lingju and Zhiyang from Jincheng, further founded Yongdeng County, and from three counties erected Guangwu Commandery.

units.zh: 張茂分武興、金城、西平、安故爲定州。
units.en: Zhang Mao raised Dingzhou from Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu.
units.literal: Zhang Mao split Wuxing, Jincheng, Xiping, and Angu to form Dingzhou.

units.zh: 張駿分武威、武興、西平、張掖、酒泉、建康、西海、西郡、湟河、晉興、廣武合十一郡爲涼州，[34]興晉、金城、武始、南安、永晉、大夏、武成、漢中爲河州，敦煌、晉昌、高昌、西域都護、戊己校尉、玉門大護軍三郡三營爲沙州。
units.en: Zhang Jun carved Liangzhou from eleven western seats,[34] stacked another eight into Hezhou, and branded three desert bases Shazhou.
units.literal: Zhang Jun organized Wuwei, Wuxing, Xiping, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Jiankang, Xihai, Xi, Huanghe, Jinxing, and Guangwu—eleven commanderies—as Liangzhou,[34] grouped Xingjin, Jincheng, Wushi, Nan'an, Yongjin, Daxia, Wucheng, and Hanzhong as Hezhou, and bundled Dunhuang, Jinchang, Gaochang, the Western Regions protector, the Wuji colonel, and Yumen grand protector—three commanderies and three camps—as Shazhou.

units.en: Note [35]: Zhang Jun governed Liangzhou pro tem over three provinces.
units.literal: [35]Zhang Jun acted as Liangzhou governor and supervised three provinces.

units.zh: 張祚又以敦煌郡爲商州。
units.en: Zhang Zuo rechristened Dunhuang as Shangzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Zuo further converted Dunhuang Commandery into Shangzhou.

units.zh: 永興中，置漢陽縣以守牧地，張玄靚改爲祁連郡。
units.en: Yongxing planted Hanyang for grazing until Zhang Xuanjing styled it Qilian Commandery.
units.literal: During Yongxing a Hanyang County was founded to guard pasturelands; Zhang Xuanjing renamed it Qilian Commandery.

units.en: Zhang Tiansi added an independent Linsong Commandery.
units.literal: Zhang Tiansi separately established Linsong Commandery.

units.zh: 天錫降於苻氏，其地尋爲呂光所據。
units.en: After Zhang Tiansi yielded to Former Qin, Lü Guang seized the corridor.
units.literal: When Tiansi surrendered to the Fu clan the territory soon fell to Lü Guang.

units.zh: 呂光都於姑臧後，以郭黁言讖，改昌松爲東張掖郡。
units.en: At Guzang Lü Guang listened to Guo Nen's omens and dubbed Changsong Eastern Zhangye.
units.literal: After Lü Guang moved his capital to Guzang he followed Guo Mo's prophecy-charts and renamed Changsong to East Zhangye Commandery.

units.zh: 及呂隆降於姚興，其地三分。
units.en: Lü Long's capitulation to Yao Xing shattered the plateau into three rivals.
units.literal: When Lü Long surrendered to Yao Xing the land split three ways.

units.zh: 武昭王爲西涼，建號於敦煌。
units.en: Prince Wuzhao's Western Liang flew its banner from Dunhuang.
units.literal: Prince Wuzhao founded Western Liang and raised his standard at Dunhuang.

units.zh: 禿髮烏孤爲南涼，建號於樂都。
units.en: Tufa Wugu styled Southern Liang from Ledu.
units.literal: Tufa Wugu founded Southern Liang and raised his standard at Ledu.

units.zh: 沮渠蒙遜爲北涼，建號於張掖。
units.en: Juqu Mengxun proclaimed Northern Liang at Zhangye.
units.literal: Juqu Mengxun founded Northern Liang and raised his standard at Zhangye.

units.en: The trio partitioned the Hexi pentarchy.
units.literal: They divided the five Hexi commanderies among themselves.

units.zh: 案禹貢本雍州之域，魏始分隴右置焉，刺史領護羌校尉，中間暫廢。
units.en: Classical Yongzhou fed Wei Longyou commands overseen by a Qiang colonel—sometimes suspended.
units.literal: By the scheme of the "Tribute of Yu" this was Yongzhou soil; Wei first carved Longyou from it; the inspector doubled as Qiang colonel until briefly abolished.

units.zh: 及泰始五年，又以雍州隴右五郡及涼州之金城、梁州之陰平，合七郡置秦州，鎮冀城。
units.en: the fifth year of Taishi welded Yongzhou's Longyou belt, Jincheng from the western Liang corridor, and Yinping from the Hanzhong Liang stack into Qinzhou at Jicheng.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi Yongzhou's Longyou quintet plus Jincheng from cool Liangzhou and Yinping from Liang-Han commandery—seven commanderies—were forged into Qinzhou with seat at Jicheng.

units.zh: 太康三年，罷秦州，并雍州。
units.en: Taikang 3 swallowed Qinzhou back into Yongzhou.
units.literal: Taikang 3 abolished Qinzhou and merged it into Yongzhou.

units.en: In the seventh year it was restored, with its seat at Shanggui.
units.literal: In the seventh year it was restored with headquarters at Shanggui.

units.zh: 統郡六，縣二十四，戶三萬二千一百。
units.en: Six commanderies, twenty-four counties, thirty-two thousand one hundred households.
units.literal: It governs six commanderies, twenty-four counties, and thirty-two thousand one hundred households.

units.en: The Longxi commandery.
units.literal: Longxi Commandery.

units.en: 〈Qin charter.
units.literal: 〈Qin established it.

units.en: Four counties and three thousand households.〉
units.literal: It governs four counties; households three thousand.〉

units.en: Xiangwu and Shouyang counties.
units.literal: Xiangwu Shouyang.

units.en: 〈Mount Niao-Wu guards the eastern skyline.〉
units.literal: 〈Mount Niao-Wu lies to the east.〉

units.en: Lintao and Didao counties.
units.literal: Lintao Didao.

units.en: The Nan'an commandery.
units.literal: Nan'an Commandery.

units.en: 〈Han foundation.
units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.en: Three counties and four thousand three hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs three counties; households four thousand three hundred.〉

units.zh: 獂道 新興 中陶
units.en: Yuandao, Xinxing, and Zhongtao counties.
units.literal: Yuandao Xinxing Zhongtao.

units.en: The Tianshui commandery.
units.literal: Tianshui Commandery.

units.zh: 〈漢武置，孝明改爲漢陽，晉復爲天水。
units.en: 〈Han Emperor Wu founded it; Emperor Ming tried Hanyang; Jin revived Tianshui.
units.literal: 〈Emperor Wu of Han founded it; Emperor Ming renamed it Hanyang; Jin restored the name Tianshui.

units.en: Gloss [36]: six counties and eight thousand five hundred households.〉
units.literal: [36]It governs six counties; households eight thousand five hundred.〉

units.en: Shanggui and Ji counties.
units.literal: Shanggui Ji.

units.en: 〈Original Qinzhou headquarters.〉
units.literal: 〈Former seat of Qinzhou.〉

units.zh: 始昌 新陽 顯新
units.en: Shichang, Xinyang, and Xianxin counties.
units.literal: Shichang Xinyang Xianxin.

units.en: 〈Han archives labeled it Xianqin.〉
units.literal: 〈Han called it Xianqin County.〉

units.en: Chengji county.
units.literal: Chengji.

units.en: The Lüeyang commandery.
units.literal: Lüeyang Commandery.

units.en: 〈Born as Guangwei Commandery until Taishi retitled it.
units.literal: 〈Originally titled Guangwei; renamed during Taishi.

units.zh: 統縣四，戶九千三百二十。〉
units.en: Four counties and nine thousand three hundred twenty households.〉
units.literal: It governs four counties; households nine thousand three hundred twenty.〉

units.zh: 臨渭 平襄 略陽 清水
units.en: Linwei, Pingxiang, Lüeyang, and Qingshui counties.
units.literal: Linwei Pingxiang Lüeyang Qingshui.

units.en: The Wudu commandery.
units.literal: Wudu Commandery.

units.en: 〈Han foundation.
units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.en: Five counties and three thousand households.〉
units.literal: It governs five counties; households three thousand.〉

units.zh: 下辯 河池 沮 武都 故道
units.en: Xiabian, Hechi, Ju, Wudu, and Gudao counties.
units.literal: Xiabian Hechi Ju Wudu Gudao.

units.en: The Yinping commandery.
units.literal: Yinping Commandery.

units.en: 〈Founded mid-Taishi.
units.literal: 〈Established mid Taishi.

units.en: Two counties and three thousand households.〉
units.literal: It governs two counties; households three thousand.〉

units.en: Yinping and Pingguang[37] counties.
units.literal: Yinping Pingguang[37].

units.zh: 惠帝分隴西之狄道、臨洮、河關，又立洮陽、遂平、武街、始興、第五、真仇六縣，合九縣置狄道郡，屬秦州。
units.en: Emperor Hui split Didao, Lintao, and Heguan from Longxi, also established the six counties Taoyang, Suiping, Wujie, Shixing, Diwu, and Zhenqiu, and from those nine counties created Didao Commandery, attaching it to Qinzhou.
units.literal: Emperor Hui split Didao, Lintao, and Heguan from Longxi, added six new counties—Taoyang, Suiping, Wujie, Shixing, Diwu, and Zhenqiu—and from nine counties formed Didao Commandery under Qinzhou.

units.zh: 張駿分屬涼州，又以狄道縣立武始郡。
units.en: Zhang Jun shifted the bundle to Liangzhou and stacked Wushi atop Didao.
units.literal: Zhang Jun reassigned it to Liangzhou and used Didao County to erect Wushi Commandery.

units.zh: 江左分梁爲秦，寄居梁州，又立氐池爲北秦州。
units.en: South of the Yangtze they split Liang into Qin, which sojourned in Liang Province, and they further established Dichi as Northern Qinzhou.
units.literal: South of the Yangtze courtiers split Liang into Qin, lodged it inside Liangzhou, and raised Dichi as Northern Qinzhou.

units.zh: 案禹貢華陽黑水之地，舜置十二牧，則其一也。
units.en: Classical Huayang country belonged to Shun's twelve pastures.
units.literal: By the Huayang Blackwater tract of the "Tribute of Yu," Shun's twelve shepherds included this belt.

units.zh: 梁者，言西方金剛之氣強梁，故因名焉。
units.en: 'Liang' evokes hard western temper—the label stuck.
units.literal: 'Liang' speaks of stern metal qi in the west—hence the name.

units.en: The Zhou Rites map paired Liang with Yong.
units.literal: The 《Zhou Rites》 Director of Regions paired Liang with Yong.

units.zh: 漢不立州名，以其地爲益州。
units.en: Han simply treated it as part of Yizhou.
units.literal: Han never titled the province; the zone counted as Yizhou.

units.zh: 及獻帝初平六年，以臨江縣屬永寧郡。
units.en: In Emperor Xian's sixth year of Chuping, Linjiang County was attached to Yongning Commandery.
units.literal: In Emperor Xian's sixth year of Chuping Linjiang County joined Yongning Commandery.

units.zh: 建安六年，劉璋改永寧爲巴東郡，分巴郡墊江置巴西郡。
units.en: In Jian'an 6 Liu Zhang renamed Yongning to Badong Commandery and split Dianjiang from Ba Commandery to create Baxi Commandery.
units.literal: Jian'an 6 Liu Zhang renamed Yongning to Badong Commandery and split Dianjiang from Ba Commandery to create Baxia Commandery.

units.zh: 劉備據蜀，又分廣漢之葭萌、涪城、梓潼、白水四縣，改葭萌曰漢壽，又立漢德縣，以爲梓潼郡；
units.en: Liu Bei carved Zitong Commandery from four Guanghan counties and rechristened Jiameng as Hanshou.
units.literal: After Liu Bei seized Shu he split Jiameng, Fucheng, Zitong, and Baishui from Guanghan—renaming Jiameng to Hanshou—and founded Hande County as Zitong Commandery;

units.zh: 割巴郡之宕渠、宣漢、漢昌三縣置宕渠郡，尋省，以縣並屬巴西郡。
units.en: Dangqu Commandery lasted briefly before its seats slid back into Ba.
units.literal: He cut Dangqu, Xuanhan, and Hanchang from Ba Commandery to plant Dangqu Commandery; soon it was abolished and the counties reverted to Ba Commandery.

units.zh: 泰始三年，分益州，立梁州於漢中，改漢壽爲晉壽，又分廣漢置新都郡。
units.en: In the third year of Taishi, Yizhou was divided, Liangzhou was established at Hanzhong, Hanshou was renamed Jinshou, and Xindu Commandery was split from Guanghan.
units.literal: the third year of Taishi split Yizhou, planted Liangzhou at Hanzhong, renamed Hanshou to Jinshou, and split Guanghan to create Xindu Commandery.

units.zh: 梁州統郡八，縣四十四，[39]戶七萬六千三百。
units.en: Eight commanderies, forty-four counties,[39] seventy-six thousand three hundred households.
units.literal: Liangzhou oversaw eight commanderies, forty-four counties,[39] and seventy-six thousand three hundred households.

units.en: The Hanzhong commandery.
units.literal: Hanzhong Commandery.

units.en: 〈Qin charter.
units.literal: 〈Qin established it.

units.en: Eight counties and fifteen thousand households.〉
units.literal: It governs eight counties; households fifteen thousand.〉

units.zh: 南鄭 蒲池 褒中 沔陽 成固 西鄉 黃金 興道
units.en: Nanzheng, Puchi, Baozhong, Mianyang, Chenggu, Xixiang, Huangjin, and Xingdao counties.
units.literal: Nanzheng Puchi Baozhong Mianyang Chenggu Xixiang Huangjin Xingdao.

units.en: The Zitong commandery.
units.literal: Zitong Commandery.

units.en: 〈Shu regime.
units.literal: 〈Shu Han established it.

units.en: Eight counties and ten thousand two hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs eight counties; households ten thousand two hundred.〉

units.zh: 梓潼 涪城 武連 黃安 漢德 晉壽 劍閣 白水
units.en: Zitong, Fucheng, Wulian, Huang'an, Hande, Jinshou, Jiange, and Baishui counties.
units.literal: Zitong Fucheng Wulian Huang'an Hande Jinshou Jiange Baishui.

units.en: The Guanghan commandery.
units.literal: Guanghan Commandery.

units.en: 〈Han foundation.
units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.en: Three counties and five thousand one hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs three counties; households five thousand one hundred.〉

units.zh: 廣漢 德陽 五城
units.en: Guanghan, Deyang, and Wucheng counties.
units.literal: Guanghan Deyang Wucheng.

units.en: The Xindu commandery.
units.literal: Xindu Commandery.

units.en: 〈the second year of Taishi creation.
units.literal: 〈Established in the second year of Taishi.

units.zh: 統縣四，戶二萬四千五百。〉
units.en: Four counties and twenty-four thousand five hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs four counties; households twenty-four thousand five hundred.〉

units.zh: 雒 什方 緜竹 新都
units.en: Luo, Shifang, Mianzhu, and Xindu counties.
units.literal: Luo Shifang Mianzhu Xindu.

units.en: The Fuling commandery.
units.literal: Fuling Commandery.

units.en: 〈Shu regime.
units.literal: 〈Shu Han established it.

units.en: Five counties and four thousand two hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs five counties; households four thousand two hundred.〉

units.zh: 漢復 涪陵 漢平 漢葭 萬寧
units.en: Hanfu, Fuling, Hanping, Hanjia, and Wanning counties.
units.literal: Hanfu Fuling Hanping Hanjia Wanning.

units.en: The Ba commandery.
units.literal: Ba Commandery.

units.en: 〈Qin charter.
units.literal: 〈Qin established it.

units.en: Four counties and three thousand three hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs four counties; households three thousand three hundred.〉

units.zh: 江州 墊江 臨江 枳
units.en: Jiangzhou, Dianjiang, Linjiang, and Zhi counties.
units.literal: Jiangzhou Dianjiang Linjiang Zhi.

units.en: The Baxi commandery.
units.literal: Baxi Commandery.

units.en: 〈Shu regime.
units.literal: 〈Shu Han established it.

units.en: Note [40]: nine counties and twelve thousand households.〉
units.literal: [40]It governs nine counties; households twelve thousand.〉

units.zh: 閬中 西充國 蒼溪 岐愜 南充國 漢昌 宕渠 安漢 平州
units.en: Langzhong, Xichongguo, Cangxi, Qiqie, Nanchongguo, Hanchang, Dangqu, Anhan, and Pingzhou counties.
units.literal: Langzhong Xichongguo Cangxi Qiqie Nanjiangguo Hanchang Dangqu Anhan Pingzhou.

units.en: The Badong commandery.
units.literal: Badong Commandery.

units.en: 〈Han foundation.
units.literal: 〈Han established it.

units.en: Three counties and six thousand five hundred households.〉
units.literal: It governs three counties; households six thousand five hundred.〉

units.en: Yufu,[41] Quyin, and Nanpu counties.
units.literal: Yufu[41] Quyin Nanpu.

units.zh: 太康六年九月，罷新都郡并廣漢郡。
units.en: Taikang 6, ninth month, folded Xindu back into Guanghan.
units.literal: Taikang 6, ninth month, abolished Xindu Commandery and merged it into Guanghan.

units.zh: 惠帝復分巴西置宕渠郡，統宕渠、漢昌、宣漢三縣，并以新城、魏興、上庸合四郡以屬梁州。
units.en: Emperor Hui revived Dangqu from Baxi and bundled four frontier commands under Liangzhou.
units.literal: Emperor Hui again split Baxi to recreate Dangqu Commandery—governing Dangqu, Hanchang, and Xuanhan—and grouped it with Xincheng, Weixing, and Shangyong into four commands under Liangzhou.

units.zh: 尋而梁州郡縣沒于李特，永嘉中又分屬楊茂搜，其晉人流寓於梁益者，仍於二州立南北二陰平郡。
units.en: Li Te swallowed Liangzhou seats; Yongjia fragments entered Yang Maosou's sphere; exiles duplicated Yinping north and south.
units.literal: Soon Liangzhou folds fell to Li Te; during Yongjia they passed piecemeal to Yang Maosou; Jin refugees drifted into Liang-Yi and spawned northern and southern Yinping commanderies.

units.zh: 及桓溫平蜀之後，以巴漢流人立晉昌郡，領長樂、安晉、延壽、安樂、宣漢、寧都、新興、吉陽、東關、永安十縣；
units.en: Huan Wen's Shu campaign yielded Jinchang Commandery with ten refugee counties.
units.literal: After Huan Wen pacified Shu he planted Jinchang Commandery for Ba-Han refugees—supervising Changle, Anjin, Yanshou, Anle, Xuanhan, Ningdu, Xinxing, Jiyang, Dongguan, and Yong'an—ten counties;

units.zh: 又置益昌、晉興二縣，屬巴西郡；
units.en: Yichang and Jinxing were placed under Baxi Commandery.
units.literal: He added Yichang and Jinxing counties under Baxi Commandery;

units.zh: 於德陽界東南置遂寧郡；
units.en: Suining appeared southeast of Deyang.
units.literal: He established Suining Commandery southeast of Deyang.

units.zh: 又於晉壽置劍閣縣，屬梁州。
units.en: The court planted Jiange County under Jinshou's Liangzhou umbrella.
units.literal: Jiange County was also founded at Jinshou and placed under Liangzhou.

units.zh: 後孝武分梓潼北界立晉壽郡，統晉壽、白水、邵歡、興安四縣；
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu peeled Jinshou Commandery from northern Zitong with four counties.
units.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu split Zitong's northern frontier to erect Jinshou Commandery, governing Jinshou, Baishui, Shaohuan, and Xing'an counties.

units.zh: 梓潼郡徙居梓潼，罷劍閣縣；
units.en: The Zitong headquarters slid homeward and Jiange vanished.
units.literal: Zitong Commandery relocated its seat to Zitong and abolished Jiange County.

units.zh: 又別置南漢中郡，分巴西、梓潼爲金山郡。
units.en: Southern Hanzhong appeared while Baxi and Zitong fed Jinshan Commandery.
units.literal: Southern Hanzhong Commandery was separately established and Ba together with Zitong yielded Jinshan Commandery.

units.zh: 及安帝時，又立新巴、汶陽二郡，又有北新巴、華陽、南陰平、北陰平四郡，其後又立巴渠、懷安、宋熙、白水、上洛、北上洛、南宕渠、懷漢、新興、安康等十郡。
units.en: Emperor An's reign stacked refugee commands until ten more prefectures cluttered the map.
units.literal: Under Emperor An there came Xinba and Wenyang commanderies, plus Northern Xinba, Huayang, southern and northern Yinping—four more—and later Baqu, Huai'an, Songxi, Baishui, Shangluo, northern Shangluo, southern Dangqu, Huaihan, Xinxing, and Ankang—ten commanderies all told.

units.zh: 案禹貢及舜十二牧俱爲梁州之域，周合梁於雍，則又爲雍州之地。
units.en: Classical Liangzhou melted into Yong once Zhou paired Liang with Yong.
units.literal: By the "Tribute of Yu" and Shun's twelve pastures this soil belonged to Liangzhou; Zhou folded Liang into Yong, so it counts as Yongzhou ground.

units.zh: 《春秋元命包》云：「參伐流爲益州，益之爲言阨也。」
units.en: The apocryphal Yuan Ming Bao says, "Shen-Wei flows aside to become Yizhou; yi means constriction."
units.literal: The Spring and Autumn Yuan Ming Bao states: "The asterism Shen-Wei flows aside to become Yizhou; yi speaks of constriction."

units.zh: 言其所在之地險阨也，亦曰疆壤益大，故以名焉。
units.en: Commentators gloss yi as perilous terrain—or ever-widening frontier.
units.literal: It refers to how precipitous the ground is; another gloss says its borders swell outward—hence the epithet.

units.zh: 始秦惠王滅蜀，置郡，以張若爲蜀守。
units.en: When Qin's King Hui swallowed Shu he parked Zhang Ruo as prefect.
units.literal: King Hui of Qin was first to extinguish Shu, install a commandery, and appoint Zhang Ruo as governor of Shu.

units.zh: 及始皇置三十六郡，蜀郡之名不改。
units.en: Even Qin Shihuang's thirty-sixfold reform kept Shu Commandery.
units.literal: When the First Emperor founded thirty-six commanderies the name Shu Commandery stayed unchanged.

units.en: Early Han knew three Ba-Shu units.
units.literal: Early Han listed Hanzhong, Ba, and Shu.

units.zh: 高祖六年，分蜀置廣漢，凡爲四郡。
units.en: Gaozu carved Guanghan from Shu for a quartet of western prefectures.
units.literal: Gaozu's sixth year split Shu to create Guanghan—four commands altogether.

units.zh: 武帝開西南夷，更置犍爲、牂柯、越巂、益州四郡，凡八郡，遂置益州統焉，益州蓋始此也。
units.en: Han Emperor Wu's Yi thrust forged eight commands before stacking them under Yizhou province.
units.literal: Emperor Wu opened the southwestern Yi and added Qianwei, Zangke, Yuexi, and Yizhou commanderies—eight in all—then instituted Yizhou province over them; Yizhou begins here.

units.zh: 及後漢，明帝以新附置永昌郡，安帝又以諸道置蜀、廣漢、犍爲三郡屬國都尉，及靈帝又以汶江、蠶陵、廣柔三縣立汶山郡。
units.en: Later Han layered Yongchang, dependent prefectures, and Wenshan onto the southwest.
units.literal: Later Han's Ming Emperor added Yongchang for new tribes; An Emperor added Shu, Guanghan, and Qianwei dependent states; Ling Emperor raised Wenshan Commandery from Wenjiang, Canling, and Guangrou counties.

units.zh: 獻帝初平元年，劉璋分巴郡立永寧郡。
units.en: Chuping 1 saw Liu Zhang peel Yongning from Ba.
units.literal: Emperor Xian's first year of Chuping Liu Zhang split Ba Commandery to plant Yongning Commandery.

units.zh: [42]建安六年，改永寧爲巴東，以巴郡爲巴西，又立涪陵郡。
units.en: The forty-second apparatus note records Jian'an 6 renaming Yongning into Badong, folding Ba into Baxi, and planting Fuling Commandery.
units.literal: Collation gloss forty-two: Jian'an 6 renamed Yongning to Badong, designated Ba as Baxi, and founded Fuling Commandery.

units.zh: 二十一年，劉備分巴郡立固陵郡。
units.en: Year twenty-one Liu Bei drew Guling Commandery out of Ba.
units.literal: Twenty-first year Liu Bei split Ba Commandery to erect Guling Commandery.

units.zh: 蜀章武元年又改固陵爲巴東郡，巴西郡爲巴郡，又分廣漢立梓潼郡，分犍爲立江陽郡，以蜀郡屬國爲漢嘉郡，以犍爲屬國爲朱提郡。
units.en: Liu Bei's Zhangwu edicts rewired Ba-Shu names across the basin.
units.literal: Shu Han Zhangwu 1 renamed Guling to Badong, Baxi back to Ba Commandery, split Guanghan for Zitong, split Qianwei for Jiangyang, converted Shu dependent state into Hanjia Commandery, and Qianwei dependent state into Zhuti Commandery.

units.zh: 劉禪建興二年，改益州郡爲建寧郡，廣漢屬國爲陰平郡，分建寧永昌立雲南郡，分建寧牂柯立興古郡，分廣漢立東廣漢郡。
units.en: In Liu Shan's Jianxing 2, Yizhou Commandery was renamed Jianning, the Guanghan dependent state became Yinping Commandery, Yunnan Commandery was formed from Jianning and Yongchang, Xinggu Commandery from Jianning and Zangke, and Eastern Guanghan Commandery from Guanghan.
units.literal: Liu Shan Jianxing 2 converted Yizhou Commandery to Jianning, Guanghan dependent state to Yinping Commandery, split Jianning and Yongchang for Yunnan Commandery, split Jianning and Zangke for Xinggu Commandery, and split Guanghan for Eastern Guanghan Commandery.

units.zh: 魏景元中，蜀平，省東廣漢郡。
units.en: Wei annexation canceled Eastern Guanghan.
units.literal: Wei Jingyuan era Shu fell and Eastern Guanghan Commandery was abolished.

units.zh: 及武帝泰始二年，分益州置梁州，以漢中屬焉。
units.en: the second year of Taishi lifted Liangzhou from Yizhou and parked Hanzhong inside.
units.literal: Emperor Wu the second year of Taishi split Yizhou to create Liangzhou with Hanzhong attached.

units.en: Year seven added Ningzhou west of Yizhou.
units.literal: Seventh year further split Yizhou to establish Ningzhou.

units.zh: 益州統郡八，縣四十四，戶十四萬九千三百。
units.en: Eight commanderies, forty-four counties, one hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred households.
units.literal: Yizhou oversees eight commanderies, forty-four counties, and one hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred households.

units.en: Wanshou, Juolan, Zhizhi,[43] Yelang, Wuxian,[44] Bingqu, Bi, and Pingyi counties.
units.literal: Wanshou Juolan Zhizhi[43] Yelang Wuxian[44] Bingqu Bi Pingyi.

units.zh: 惠帝之後，李特僭號於蜀，稱漢，益州郡縣皆沒于特。
units.en: Post-Hui turmoil let Li Te seize Han titles across Yizhou.
units.literal: After Emperor Hui, Li Te arrogated Han rule in Shu and every Yizhou seat fell to him.

units.zh: 李雄又分漢嘉、蜀二郡立沈黎、漢原二郡。
units.en: Li Xiong peeled Shenli and Hanyuan from Hanjia and Shu.
units.literal: Li Xiong further split Hanjia and Shu to erect Shenli and Hanyuan commanderies.

units.zh: 是時益州郡縣雖沒李氏，江左並遙置之。
units.en: Courtiers beyond the river maintained empty registers.
units.literal: Though Li clan maps swallowed Yizhou, exiles south of the Yangtze kept phantom postings.

units.zh: 桓溫滅蜀，其地復爲晉有，省漢原、沈黎而立南陰平、晉原、寧蜀、始寧四郡焉。
units.en: When Huan Wen extinguished Shu, the land again belonged to Jin; Hanyuan and Shenli were abolished and southern Yinping, Jinyuan, Ningshu, and Shining commanderies were established.
units.literal: When Huan Wen extinguished Shu, Jin recovered the soil, abolished Hanyuan and Shenli, and founded southern Yinping, Jinyuan, Ningshu, and Shining commanderies.

units.zh: 咸安二年，益州復沒於苻氏。
units.en: Xian'an 2 handed Yizhou back to Former Qin.
units.literal: Xian'an 2 lost Yizhou again to the Fu clan.

units.en: Taiyuan 8 returned the basin to Jin.
units.literal: Taiyuan 8 Jin recovered it.

units.zh: 隆安二年，又立晉熙、遂寧、晉寧三郡云。
units.en: Long'an 2 raised Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning.
units.literal: Long'an 2 founded Jinxi, Suining, and Jinning commanderies.

units.en: Han-Wei archives label it Yizhou.
units.literal: Under Han and Wei this counted as Yizhou territory.

units.zh: 泰始七年，武帝以益州地廣，分益州之建寧、興古、雲南、交州之永昌，合四郡爲寧州，統縣四十五，戶八萬三千。
units.en: In the seventh year of Taishi, Emperor Wu, because Yizhou was vast, combined Jianning, Xinggu, and Yunnan from Yizhou with Yongchang from Jiao Province as Ningzhou, governing forty-five counties and eighty-three thousand households.
units.literal: the seventh year of Taishi Emperor Wu split vast Yizhou: Jianning, Xinggu, Yunnan from Yizhou plus Yongchang from Jiao Province—four commands—became Ningzhou with forty-five counties and eighty-three thousand households.

units.en: Buwei, Yongshou, Bisu, Yongxiang, Nanfu, Zuitang, Ailao, and Bonan counties.
units.literal: Buwei Yongshou Bisu Yongxiang Nanfu Zuitang Ailao Bonan.

units.zh: 太康三年，武帝又廢寧州入益州，立南夷校尉以護之。
units.en: Taikang 3 folded Ningzhou back into Yizhou under a southern Yi colonel.
units.literal: Taikang 3 Emperor Wu abolished Ningzhou into Yizhou and planted a southern Yi colonel to oversee it.

units.zh: 太安二年，惠帝復置寧州，又分建寧以西七縣別立爲益州郡。
units.en: Tai'an 2 revived Ningzhou and spawned another Yizhou Commandery west of Jianning.
units.literal: Tai'an 2 Emperor Hui restored Ningzhou and split seven counties west of Jianning into a separate Yizhou Commandery.

units.zh: 永嘉二年，改益州郡曰晉寧，分牂柯立平夷、夜郎二郡。
units.en: Yongjia 2 rechristened Yizhou Commandery as Jinning and bisected Zangke.
units.literal: Yongjia 2 renamed Yizhou Commandery to Jinning and split Zangke into Pingyi and Yelang commanderies.

units.en: [47] Yet by then the territory was again in Li Te's possession.
units.literal: Collation gloss forty-seven: yet by then Li Te again owned the ground.

units.zh: 其後李壽分寧州興古、永昌、雲南、朱提、越巂、河陽六郡爲漢州。
units.en: Li Shou carved Hanzhou from six southern commands.
units.literal: Later Li Shou split six Ningzhou commands—Xinggu, Yongchang, Yunnan, Zhuti, Yuexi, Heyang—into Hanzhou.

units.zh: 咸康四年，分牂柯、夜郎、朱提、越巂四郡置安州。
units.en: Xiankang 4 stacked Anzhou atop four frontier commands.
units.literal: Xiankang 4 organized Anzhou from Zangke, Yelang, Zhuti, and Yuexi.

units.zh: 八年，又罷并寧州，以越巂還屬益州，省永昌郡焉。
units.en: Eight years later Jin dissolved Anzhou, reassigned Yuexi, and struck Yongchang.
units.literal: Year eight abolished it back into Ningzhou, returned Yuexi to Yizhou, and abolished Yongchang Commandery.
